label: thm:universal-p-to-polyspdp
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{thm:universal-p-to-polyspdp}
Fix any deterministic Turing machine $M\in\mathrm{DTIME}(n^t)$.
There exists a \emph{uniform}, \emph{input-independent} compiler
$\Compdet$ producing a multilinear polynomial $P_{M,n}$ over a field $\F$
(of characteristic $0$, or prime $p$ sufficiently large), such that:

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item (\textbf{Uniformity}) $P_{M,n}$ is computable from the finite description of $M$
and $n$ in time $\poly(n)$ (no dependence on the particular input $x$).
\item (\textbf{Locality}) $P_{M,n}$ is assembled from constant-radius ($r=1$) local gadgets
arranged in a time$\times$tape (or layered-wire) layout.
\item (\textbf{Bounded interface types by construction}) in every canonical window,
only $O(1)$ gadget types occur, so the induced profile alphabet is finite and
\emph{independent of the window length} $\kappa$.
\item (\textbf{CEW bound}) $\CEW(P_{M,n}) = O(\log n)$.
\item (\textbf{SPDP rank bound}) for $\kappa'=\alpha\log n$ and $\ell'=\beta\log n$
(with fixed constants $\alpha,\beta>0$),
\[
\Gamma_{\kappa',\ell'}(P_{M,n})\ \le\ n^{O(1)}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, every language in $P$ admits a polynomial-SPDP-rank representation.
statement_text: Fix any deterministic Turing machine M ∈ DTIME (n^t) . There exists a uniform , input-independent compiler C _ det producing a multilinear polynomial P_ M,n over a field F (of characteristic 0 , or prime p sufficiently large), such that: (bf Uniformity ) P_ M,n is computable from the finite description of M and n in time poly (n) (no dependence on the particular input x ). (bf Locality ) P_ M,n is assembled from constant-radius ( r=1 ) local gadgets arranged in a time × tape (or layered-wire) layout. (bf Bounded interface types by construction ) in every canonical window, only O(1) gadget types occur, so the induced profile alphabet is finite and independent of the window length κ . (bf CEW bound ) CEW (P_ M,n ) = O( log n) . (bf SPDP rank bound ) for κ'=α log n and ell '=β log n (with fixed constants α,β>0 ), \[ Γ_ κ',ell ' (P_ M,n )\ ≤ \ n^ O(1) . \] Consequently, every language in P admits a polynomial-SPDP-rank representation.
title: Universal P → poly--SPDP bridge

label: lem:uniform-bounded-profile-diversity
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{lem:uniform-bounded-profile-diversity}
Let $\varphi$ be any constraint object whose incidence graph has bounded degree
$\Delta=O(1)$ and bounded arity/width $w=O(1)$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:compiler-bounded-degree}).
Fix a canonical-window rule that selects a radius-$R$ neighborhood $W(v)$ around an

\]
uniformly over all $\varphi$ and all choices of $v$, and independent of the SPDP
derivative parameter $\kappa$.

label: thm:universal-p-to-spdp-consolidated
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{thm:universal-p-to-spdp-consolidated}
For every deterministic polynomial-time Turing machine
$M \in \mathrm{DTIME}(n^t)$, the self-contained deterministic compiler
of Theorem~\ref{thm:self-contained-det-compiler}
produces an SPDP polynomial $P_{M,n}$ such that:

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \textbf{Object identity:} $P_{M,n}$ coincides with the SPDP polynomial object used in the
Codimension/Collapse Theorem (the compiled polynomial is the same mathematical object
analyzed for rank bounds).

\item \textbf{CEW implies SPDP-admissibility:} The CEW bound $\mathrm{CEW}(P_{M,n}) = O(\log n)$
implies $P_{M,n}\in\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{coll}}(n)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:cew-to-admissible}.

\item \textbf{Rank collapse:} Consequently, for the parameter regime of
Theorem~\ref{thm:collapse-for-class} (in particular $\kappa=\Theta(\log n)$ and
$\ell$ as specified there),
\[
\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(P_{M,n}) \le n^{O(1)}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

Thus, the universal inclusion
\[
P \subseteq \mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{coll}}
\]
holds in ZFC, with all quantifiers discharged by explicit uniform construction.

statement_tex:
Let $p\in\mathbb{F}[x_1,\ldots,x_N]$ with a partition $\mathcal{B}=\{B_1,\ldots,B_m\}$ of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ into blocks of size $\le b=O(1)$.
Fix $\kappa,\ell\in\mathbb{N}$. Rows are indexed by pairs $(\tau,u)$ with $|\tau|=\kappa$, $u\in\mathrm{Mon}_{\le \ell}$, and
\[
\mathrm{supp\_blocks}(\tau):=\{j:\exists i\in B_j,\ \tau_i>0\}

\qquad

\]

statement_tex:
\label{thm:np-identity-minor-formal}
Let $F$ be a field of characteristic $0$ or prime $p > \mathrm{poly}(n)$. Let

Q_{\Phi_n}^{\times}(u,z) = \prod_{C \in \Phi_n} \bigl(1 - z_C \cdot V_C(u)^2\bigr)

\]
The identity-minor construction uses the multiplicative coupling structure which preserves cross-block mixed partials (unlike the additive formulation; see Remark~\ref{rem:why-coupled}).

\label{def:template-partition}

where every $T\in\mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{ver}}$ uses only verification/interface variables

(e.g.\ $v$).  No template contains both $(u,z)$ and $v$ variables in the same gadget.

\label{lem:additive-separability}

such that

\]
and $V_{M,n}$ contains no $v$-variables while $R_{M,n}$ contains no $(u,z)$-variables.
In particular, $P_{M,n}$ has no mixed monomials involving both $(u,z)$ and $v$.

In particular, P_ M,n has no mixed monomials involving both (u,z) and v .

label: thm:tphi-formal
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{thm:tphi-formal}
For every 3SAT instance $\Phi$ with $n$ variables,
there exists a block-local transformation
\[
T_\Phi = (\text{basis}) \circ (\text{affine relabeling}) \circ (\text{restriction}) \circ (\text{projection})
\]
such that
\[
T_\Phi(P_{M^*,|\rho(\Phi)|}) = Q^{\times}_\Phi,
\quad
\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(T_\Phi(\cdot)) \leq \Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(\cdot).
\]
Moreover, $T_\Phi$ is \textbf{uniformly computable} with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \textbf{Time bound:} The description of $T_\Phi$ can be computed from $\Phi$ in time $\mathrm{poly}(n)$.
\item \textbf{Description length:} The representation of $T_\Phi$ has size $\mathrm{poly}(n)$.
\item \textbf{Instance-independence:} The structure of $T_\Phi$ depends only on the size $n$ and parameters $(\kappa,\ell)$, not on the specific satisfying assignment or accepting computation. The map is determined entirely by the clause structure of $\Phi$ and the fixed compiler templates from Section~\ref{sec:tm-arithmetization}.
\item \textbf{Rank monotonicity:} Each stage (basis change, affine relabeling, restriction, projection) preserves or decreases SPDP rank by Lemma~\ref{lem:monotonicity-suite}; see also Lemma~\ref{lem:god-move-properties} for the combined God-move properties.
\end{enumerate}

statement_tex:
\label{def:collapsing-class}
Fix parameters $\kappa=\lceil \alpha \log n\rceil$ and $\ell=\lceil \beta \log n\rceil$.
A multilinear polynomial $p$ over $N=\poly(n)$ variables is in
$\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{coll}}(n)$ if there exists a \emph{canonical window}
decomposition and \emph{interface-anonymous profile} representation satisfying:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \textbf{Local canonical windows:} $p$ decomposes into local windows of
radius $O(1)$ after the canonicalization map of
Section~\ref{sec:canonical-windows}.

\item \textbf{Bounded interface diversity:} within each window, the number of
realizable interface-anonymous profiles is at most $n^{O(1)}$ (equivalently,
profile compression removes any $\kappa$-dependence as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:profile-compression-removes-k}).

\item \textbf{SPDP-admissibility:} the induced feature scheme is SPDP-admissible
in the sense of Definition~\ref{def:spdp-admissible-feature-scheme}
(and hence satisfies the Codimension/Collapse hypotheses).

\end{enumerate}

\label{thm:uniform-p-to-spdp}

\[

\[

\]

label: lem:np-complete-witness-bookkeeping
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{lem:np-complete-witness-bookkeeping}
Let $\mathrm{3SAT}\subseteq\{0,1\}^\ast$ denote the standard NP-complete
language of satisfiable 3-CNF formulas under the usual binary encoding
(e.g.\ listing clauses as triples of signed variable indices). Let
$\{\Phi_n\}$ be the explicit 3-CNF family used in
Section~\ref{sec:godmove} (e.g.\ the expander/Tseitin/Ramanujan--Tseitin
construction), with $|\Phi_n|=\poly(n)$ and each $\Phi_n$ a bona fide 3-CNF
formula over $n$ primary variables and $\poly(n)$ auxiliary variables.

Then:

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \textbf{$\Phi_n$ is a standard 3SAT instance.}
For every $n$, the formula $\Phi_n$ is a syntactically valid 3-CNF formula,
and its encoding length satisfies $|\enc(\Phi_n)|=\poly(n)$.

\item \textbf{Uniform constructibility.}
The map $n\mapsto \enc(\Phi_n)$ is computable in time $\poly(n)$ (indeed
logspace/uniform, if desired), so $\{\Phi_n\}$ forms an explicit uniform family
of inputs to $\mathrm{3SAT}$.

\item \textbf{Same encoding regime for SPDP objects.}
Let $\Comp$ be the uniform compiler/encoding map fixed in
Theorem~\ref{thm:uniform-p-to-spdp} (or Theorem~\ref{thm:universal-p-to-spdp-consolidated}).
Define the NP-side SPDP object by
\[
q_n \;:=\; \Comp(\Phi_n).
\]
Then $q_n$ is exactly the SPDP polynomial associated to the standard 3SAT input
$\Phi_n$ under the \emph{same} compilation/feature-scheme/canonical-window
regime used on the P-side.

\item \textbf{NP-complete witness role.}
Consequently, any claimed separation that proves a rank lower bound for the
family $\{q_n\}$ (e.g.\ $\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(q_n)\ge n^{\Omega(\log n)}$ for
$\kappa,\ell=\Theta(\log n)$) is a rank lower bound for a uniform family of
\emph{standard 3SAT instances} under the paper's fixed encoding.
\end{enumerate}
statement_text: Let 3SAT ⊆ {0,1}^ast denote the standard NP-complete language of satisfiable 3-CNF formulas under the usual binary encoding (e.g.\ listing clauses as triples of signed variable indices). Let {Φ_n} be the explicit 3-CNF family used in Section (e.g.\ the expander/Tseitin/Ramanujan--Tseitin construction), with |Φ_n|= poly (n) and each Φ_n a bona fide 3-CNF formula over n primary variables and poly (n) auxiliary variables. Then: bf Φ_n is a standard 3SAT instance. For every n , the formula Φ_n is a syntactically valid 3-CNF formula, and its encoding length satisfies | enc (Φ_n)|= poly (n) . bf Uniform constructibility. The map nmapsto enc (Φ_n) is computable in time poly (n) (indeed logspace/uniform, if desired), so {Φ_n} forms an explicit uniform family of inputs to 3SAT . bf Same encoding regime for SPDP objects. Let C be the uniform compiler/encoding map fixed in Theorem (or Theorem ). Define the NP-side SPDP object by \[ q_n := C (Φ_n). \] Then q_n is exactly the SPDP polynomial associated to the standard 3SAT input Φ_n under the same compilation/feature-scheme/canonical-window regime used on the P-side. bf NP-complete witness role. Consequently, any claimed separation that proves a rank lower bound for the family {q_n} (e.g.\ Γ_ κ,ell (q_n) ≥ n^ Ω( log n) for κ,ell =Θ( log n) ) is a rank lower bound for a uniform family of standard 3SAT instances under the paper's fixed encoding.
title: NP-completeness bookkeeping for the witness family

label: thm:godmove-formal
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{thm:godmove-formal}
Fix $\kappa=\lceil K\log n\rceil$ and $\ell=\lceil \beta\log n\rceil$ for constants $K,\beta>0$.

Assume for contradiction that $P=NP$. Then for the verifier-restricted machine $M'$
deciding 3SAT, the compiled polynomial satisfies

\noindent\textbf{Guard (no extraction from $\Phi$ alone).}
The extraction operator $T_{\Phi}$ is applied only to the \emph{compiled machine-exact} polynomial
$P_{M',n}$ produced by the assumed polytime decider $M'$ on input length $n$; it is not an
operator that outputs $Q^{\times}_{\Phi}$ from $\Phi$ in isolation.

The compiled polynomial satisfies
\[
\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(P_{M',n}) \le n^{O(1)}
\]
by the P-side width$\Rightarrow$rank upper bound (Theorem~\ref{thm:width-to-rank-formal}).

By the coupled extraction map (Lemma~\ref{lem:additive-separability}),
\[
\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}\!\big(Q^{\times}_{\Phi_n}\big)
\ \le\ \Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(P_{M',n})
\ \le\ n^{O(1)}.
\]

On the other hand, by the coefficient-space identity minor for coupled sheets
(Theorem~\ref{thm:np-identity-minor-formal}, which applies to $Q^{\times}_{\Phi_n}$),
\[
\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}\!\big(Q^{\times}_{\Phi_n}\big)\ \ge\ n^{\Theta(\log n)},
\]
a contradiction for large $n$. Hence $P\neq NP$.
statement_text: Fix κ=lceil K log nrceil and ell =lceil β log nrceil for constants K,β>0 . Assume for contradiction that P=NP . Then for the verifier-restricted machine M' deciding 3SAT, the compiled polynomial satisfies bf Guard (no extraction from Φ alone). The extraction operator T_ Φ is applied only to the compiled machine-exact polynomial P_ M',n produced by the assumed polytime decider M' on input length n ; it is not an operator that outputs Q^ × _ Φ from Φ in isolation. The compiled polynomial satisfies \[ Γ_ κ,ell (P_ M',n ) ≤ n^ O(1) \] by the P-side width ⇒ rank upper bound (Theorem ). By the coupled extraction map (Lemma ), \[ Γ_ κ,ell (Q^ × _ Φ_n ) \ ≤ \ Γ_ κ,ell (P_ M',n ) \ ≤ \ n^ O(1) . \] On the other hand, by the coefficient-space identity minor for coupled sheets (Theorem , which applies to Q^ × _ Φ_n ), \[ Γ_ κ,ell (Q^ × _ Φ_n )\ ≥ \ n^ Θ( log n) , \] a contradiction for large n . Hence P ≠ NP .
title: Global God-Move ⇒ P ≠ NP (coupled-sheet form)

label: thm:uniform-extraction-verifier-sos
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{thm:uniform-extraction-verifier-sos}
There exists a deterministic, instance-uniform map
\[
\mathcal{E} : (\Phi, M) \longmapsto (Q^{\times}_\Phi, P_{M,n})
\]
with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{P-side compilation.} For any polytime decider $M$ of 3SAT, the compiler produces $P_{M,n}$ with
\[
\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(P_{M,n}) \leq n^{O(1)}, \quad \kappa, \ell = \Theta(\log n).
\]

\item \textbf{Verifier extraction.} For each 3SAT instance $\Phi$ with $n$ variables and $m$ clauses, the map extracts $Q^{\times}_\Phi$ (the coupled clause-gadget SoS polynomial, Definition~\ref{def:Qphi-times}) such that
\[
\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(Q^{\times}_\Phi) \leq \Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(P_{M,n}) \leq n^{O(1)}.
\]

\item \textbf{Block-locality.} The extraction $T_\Phi : P_{M,n} \mapsto Q^{\times}_\Phi$ decomposes as a finite composition of block-local operations (restriction, projection, affine relabeling, basis change), each operating within radius $O(1)$ blocks.

\item \textbf{NP-side lower bound.} For sufficiently hard 3SAT instances $\Phi_n$ (derived from the permanent via Valiant--Vazirani reduction or direct construction),
\[
\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(Q^{\times}_{\Phi_n}) \geq n^{\Theta(\log n)}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
statement_text: There exists a deterministic, instance-uniform map \[ E : (Φ, M) longmapsto (Q^ × _Φ, P_ M,n ) \] with the following properties: bf P-side compilation. For any polytime decider M of 3SAT, the compiler produces P_ M,n with \[ Γ_ κ,ell (P_ M,n ) ≤ n^ O(1) , quad κ, ell = Θ( log n). \] bf Verifier extraction. For each 3SAT instance Φ with n variables and m clauses, the map extracts Q^ × _Φ (the coupled clause-gadget SoS polynomial, Definition ) such that \[ Γ_ κ,ell (Q^ × _Φ) ≤ Γ_ κ,ell (P_ M,n ) ≤ n^ O(1) . \] bf Block-locality. The extraction T_Φ : P_ M,n mapsto Q^ × _Φ decomposes as a finite composition of block-local operations (restriction, projection, affine relabeling, basis change), each operating within radius O(1) blocks. bf NP-side lower bound. For sufficiently hard 3SAT instances Φ_n (derived from the permanent via Valiant--Vazirani reduction or direct construction), \[ Γ_ κ,ell (Q^ × _ Φ_n ) ≥ n^ Θ( log n) . \]
title: Uniform Block-Local Extraction of the Verifier SoS

statement_text: Fix the compiler template family Comp (radius-- 1 blocks, diagonal basis, and Π^+ ). We write p equiv _ comp p' (or p p' ) if p' is obtained from p by a finite sequence of the following moves (and their inverses where applicable): bf (E1) Block-local invertible changes. Blockwise invertible linear changes of variables within blocks, and block-local variable renamings (permutations) consistent with the block partition B . bf (E2) Tag specialization / administrative normalization. Deterministic specialization, coalescing, or elimination of administrative tags introduced by the compiler front-end, in a way that preserves the Boolean semantics of the compiled instance. bf (E3) Deletion of identically-zero components (only). Removal of constraints/cells whose compiled polynomial is identically 0 after deterministic normalization. No other notion of ``semantically inactive'' is permitted. bf (E4) Commutation / reordering of independent cells. Reordering (permutation) of commuting factors, independent cells, or disjoint local constraints, including deterministic tie-breaking conventions. bf (E6) Positive-cone closure Π^+ . Applying the canonical ``positive-cone'' linear map Π^+ used in the final canonicalization layer. By definition of the compiler, Π^+ is chosen block-local and invertible on each block, hence is a special case of (E1) (recorded separately because it is used repeatedly in the narrative).
title: Compiler equivalence moves

statement_tex:

\]
where $\sigma^2 = \text{Var}(X)$.

paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{def:spdp-appg}
Let $p\in\Bbb F[x_1,\ldots,x_N]$ and let $\mathcal B=\{B_1,\ldots,B_m\}$ be a partition of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ into blocks of size $\le b=O(1)$.
Fix $\kappa,\ell\in\Bbb N$. Rows are indexed by pairs $(\tau,u)$ with multi-index $\tau\in\Bbb N^N$ of weight $|\tau|=\kappa$ whose block support
$\,\mathrm{supp}_{\mathcal B}(\tau):=\{j:\exists i\in B_j,\ \tau_i>0\}$ satisfies $|\mathrm{supp}_{\mathcal B}(\tau)|\le \kappa$, and $u$ a monomial of degree $\le \ell$.
Columns are monomials $x^\beta$ with $\deg x^\beta \le \deg(p)-\kappa+\ell$ (empty set if negative).
Define
\[
M^{\mathcal B}_{\kappa,\ell}(p)\big[(\tau,u),x^\beta\big]
:= \mathrm{coeff}_{x^\beta}\!\big(u\cdot \partial^\tau p\big),
\qquad
\Gamma^{\mathcal B}_{\kappa,\ell}(p):=\mathrm{rank}_\Bbb F\big(M^{\mathcal B}_{\kappa,\ell}(p)\big).
\]
statement_text: Let p ∈ Bbb F[x_1, ... ,x_N] and let B={B_1, ... ,B_m} be a partition of {1, ... ,N} into blocks of size ≤ b=O(1) . Fix κ,ell ∈ Bbb N . Columns are monomials x^β with deg x^β ≤ deg (p)-κ+ell (empty set if negative). Define \[ M^ B _ κ,ell (p) [(τ,u),x^β ] := coeff _ x^β (u · partial ^τ p ), qquad Γ^ B _ κ,ell (p):= rank _Bbb F (M^ B _ κ,ell (p) ). \]

label: lem:isolator
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{lem:isolator}
Let $N$ be the number of clause--blocks/variable--pads in $Q_{\Phi_n}$ and let $\kappa=\alpha\log n$ for a fixed $\alpha>0$.
There exists a family $\mathcal{H}$ of $\kappa$-perfect hash functions $h:[N]\to[\kappa]$ of size
\[
|\mathcal{H}| \;\le\; C_0\, \kappa^\kappa \log N \;=\; n^{O(1)}
\]
with the following property: for every $\kappa$-subset $S\subseteq[N]$ there is an $h\in\mathcal{H}$ that is injective on $S$.
For each $S$ choose the unique monomial $x^{\beta(S)}$ that selects, in the SoS clause gadget for $Q_{\Phi_n}$, exactly the $\kappa$ literal--wires indexed by $S$ and no others (feasible because each block exposes private pads and the gadgets are block-separable). Then the SPDP submatrix with rows indexed by the $\kappa$-tuples $S$ and columns by the $x^{\beta(S)}$ is the identity.
Consequently,
\[
\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}\!\big(Q_{\Phi_n}\big)\;\ge\;\binom{N}{\kappa}
\;=\; n^{\Theta(\log n)} .
\]
statement_text: Let N be the number of clause--blocks/variable--pads in Q_ Φ_n and let κ=α log n for a fixed α>0 . There exists a family H of κ -perfect hash functions h:[N] → [κ] of size \[ | H | ≤ C_0 κ^κ log N = n^ O(1) \] with the following property: for every κ -subset S ⊆ [N] there is an h ∈ H that is injective on S . For each S choose the unique monomial x^ β(S) that selects, in the SoS clause gadget for Q_ Φ_n , exactly the κ literal--wires indexed by S and no others (feasible because each block exposes private pads and the gadgets are block-separable). Then the SPDP submatrix with rows indexed by the κ -tuples S and columns by the x^ β(S) is the identity. Consequently, \[ Γ_ κ,ell (Q_ Φ_n ) ≥ binom N κ = n^ Θ( log n) . \]

label: lem:identity-minor-explicit
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{lem:identity-minor-explicit}
Let $\Phi_n$ be the Ramanujan--Tseitin instance on a fixed $d$-regular
expander $G_n = (V_n,E_n)$ with $|V_n| = m$ and $|E_n| = N = \Theta(n)$, and
let $p_n$ be the associated multilinear polynomial in edge-variables
$\{x_e : e \in E_n\}$ constructed above. For
parameters $\kappa = \alpha \log n$ and $\ell = \beta \log n$ as in the main text, there exist:
\begin{itemize}
  \item a set $R$ of $\binom{N}{\kappa} = n^{\Theta(\log n)}$ SPDP rows, indexed by
  mixed partials $\partial^{\tau}$ concentrating on $\kappa$-tuples of vertices
  with pairwise disjoint neighbourhoods, and
  \item a matching set $C$ of $\binom{N}{\kappa}$ columns, indexed by monomials
  $x^{\alpha}$ selecting one incident edge per such vertex,
\end{itemize}
such that the submatrix $M(p_n)[R,C]$ is a signed identity matrix. In
particular, $\operatorname{rank} M(p_n) \ge \binom{N}{\kappa}$ and there are no
cancellations among the corresponding monomials.
statement_text: Let Φ_n be the Ramanujan--Tseitin instance on a fixed d -regular expander G_n = (V_n,E_n) with |V_n| = m and |E_n| = N = Θ(n) , and let p_n be the associated multilinear polynomial in edge-variables {x_e : e ∈ E_n} constructed above. label: def:spdp-matrix-formal
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{def:spdp-matrix-formal}\label{def:spdp-matrix}
Let $\mathbb{F}$ be a field and $p \in \mathbb{F}[x_1, \ldots, x_N]$ a polynomial. Fix parameters $\kappa, \ell \in \mathbb{N}$ with $\kappa \leq N$. Define:
\begin{itemize}
\item $\mathcal{S}_\kappa := \{S \subseteq [N] : |S| = \kappa\}$ (the set of all $\kappa$-subsets of variable indices),
\item $\mathcal{T}_\ell := \{\text{monomials } m \text{ in } x_1, \ldots, x_N : \deg m \leq \ell\}$,
\item For $S \in \mathcal{S}_\kappa$, define the partial derivative operator $\partial_S := \prod_{i \in S} \frac{\partial}{\partial x_i}$,
\item For $m \in \mathcal{T}_\ell$, define the shift operator $x^m : p \mapsto m \cdot p$.
\end{itemize}
The \textbf{SPDP matrix} $M_{\kappa,\ell}(p)$ is the matrix with rows indexed by $(S, m) \in \mathcal{S}_\kappa \times \mathcal{T}_\ell$ and columns indexed by monomials in the standard monomial basis, where the $(S,m)$-th row is the coefficient vector of $m \cdot \partial_S p$ expressed as a linear combination of monomials.

The \textbf{SPDP rank} is defined as
\[
\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(p) := \operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb{F}} M_{\kappa,\ell}(p).
\]
statement_text: Let F be a field and p ∈ F [x_1, ... , x_N] a polynomial. Fix parameters κ, ell ∈ N with κ ≤ N . Define: S _κ := {S ⊆ [N] : |S| = κ} (the set of all κ -subsets of variable indices), T _ell := { monomials m in x_1, ... , x_N : deg m ≤ ell } , For S ∈ S _κ , define the partial derivative operator partial _S := Π _ i ∈ S frac partial partial x_i , For m ∈ T _ell , define the shift operator x^m : p mapsto m · p . The bf SPDP matrix M_ κ,ell (p) is the matrix with rows indexed by (S, m) ∈ S _κ × T _ell and columns indexed by monomials in the standard monomial basis, where the (S,m) -th row is the coefficient vector of m · partial _S p expressed as a linear combination of monomials. The bf SPDP rank is defined as \[ Γ_ κ,ell (p) := rank _ F M_ κ,ell (p). \]
title: SPDP matrix

label: def:cew-formal
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{def:cew-formal}
Let $p$ be a polynomial representing a Boolean function or circuit. The \textbf{Contextual Entanglement Width} $\mathrm{CEW}(p)$ is the minimal $w$ such that after a universal restriction $\rho_\star$ (defined via deterministic switching lemma), the SPDP rank satisfies
\[
\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(p \!\upharpoonright\! \rho_\star) \leq w
\]
for fixed parameters $(\kappa,\ell) = \Theta(\log n)$.

For compositional systems (e.g., layered circuits), CEW satisfies the \textbf{additive composition law}:
\[
\mathrm{CEW}(f \circ g) \leq \mathrm{CEW}(f) + \mathrm{CEW}(g) + O(1),
\]
where the $O(1)$ accounts for interface gadgets.
statement_text: Let p be a polynomial representing a Boolean function or circuit. The bf Contextual Entanglement Width CEW (p) is the minimal w such that after a universal restriction ρ_star (defined via deterministic switching lemma), the SPDP rank satisfies \[ Γ_ κ,ell (p upharpoonright ρ_star ) ≤ w \] for fixed parameters (κ,ell ) = Θ( log n) . For compositional systems (e.g., layered circuits), CEW satisfies the bf additive composition law : \[ CEW (f ∘ g) ≤ CEW (f) + CEW (g) + O(1), \] where the O(1) accounts for interface gadgets.
title: CEW and additive composition law

label: def:batcher-network
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_text: The bf Batcher sorting network for N inputs is a fixed comparison network defined recursively: bf Base case : For N = 1 , the network is trivial (identity). bf Recursive case : For N > 1 , split into two halves of size lceil N/2 rceil and lfloor N/2 rfloor , recursively sort each half, then merge using the odd--even merge gadget. The network has: bf Depth : D(N) = O( log ^2 N) , bf Width : Constant (each comparison gate operates on exactly 2 wires), bf Size : S(N) = O(N log ^2 N) comparisons.
title: Batcher odd--even merge network

statement_text: Under the compiler setting of Section (bounded type set |T|=O(1) , radius-- 1 locality, and at most R= polylog (n) live interfaces throughout the sweep), the compiled SPDP rank satisfies \[ Γ^ B _ κ,ell (p) ≤ R^ O(1) = ( log n)^ O(1) quad for (κ,ell )=Θ( log n). \]
title: Compiled Width ⇒ Rank via profile compression (load-bearing)

label: lem:restriction-monotonicity
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{lem:restriction-monotonicity}
Let $p \in \mathbb{F}[x_1, \ldots, x_N]$ and $\rho : \mathbb{F}^N \to \mathbb{F}^{N'}$ be a restriction (fixing some variables to constants). Then
\[
\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(p \!\upharpoonright\! \rho) \leq \Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(p).
\]
statement_text: Let p ∈ F [x_1, ... , x_N] and ρ : F ^N → F ^ N' be a restriction (fixing some variables to constants). Then \[ Γ_ κ,ell (p upharpoonright ρ) ≤ Γ_ κ,ell (p). \]
title: Restriction monotonicity

label: lem:submatrix-monotonicity
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{lem:submatrix-monotonicity}
If $M'$ is a submatrix of $M_{\kappa,\ell}(p)$ obtained by selecting a subset of rows, then
\[
\operatorname{rank}(M') \leq \Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(p).
\]
statement_text: If M' is a submatrix of M_ κ,ell (p) obtained by selecting a subset of rows, then \[ rank (M') ≤ Γ_ κ,ell (p). \]
title: Submatrix monotonicity

label: lem:basis-Piplus-invariance
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{lem:basis-Piplus-invariance}\label{lem:affine-map-invariance}
Let $p \in \Bbb F[x_1,\ldots,x_N]$ and fix $\kappa,\ell$.
Suppose a block-local change of variables $x \mapsto Ax+b$ acts on each block by an
invertible linear map $A$ (so $\det A \neq 0$ on each block), and let $\Pi^+$ denote the
fixed positive-cone map used in the compilation (acting block-locally and invertibly on the
column space induced by the local basis).
Then left/right multiplication of $M_{\kappa,\ell}(p)$ by the corresponding
block-diagonal change-of-basis matrices is invertible, hence
\[
\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(p) \;=\; \Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}\!\big(p\circ(Ax+b)\big) \;=\; \Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}\!\big(\Pi^+[p]\big).
\]
statement_text: Let p ∈ Bbb F[x_1, ... ,x_N] and fix κ,ell . Suppose a block-local change of variables x mapsto Ax+b acts on each block by an invertible linear map A (so det A ≠ 0 on each block), and let Π^+ denote the fixed positive-cone map used in the compilation (acting block-locally and invertibly on the column space induced by the local basis). Then left/right multiplication of M_ κ,ell (p) by the corresponding block-diagonal change-of-basis matrices is invertible, hence \[ Γ_ κ,ell (p) = Γ_ κ,ell (p ∘ (Ax+b) ) = Γ_ κ,ell (Π^+[p] ). \]
title: Block-local affine/basis invariance and Π^+

label: lem:basis-invariance-appg
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{lem:basis-invariance-appg}
The rank $\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(p)$ does not depend on the choice of monomial ordering or coordinate system (up to linear isomorphism).
statement_text: The rank Γ_ κ,ell (p) does not depend on the choice of monomial ordering or coordinate system (up to linear isomorphism).

statement_tex:

label: lem:k-injective-family
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{lem:k-injective-family}
Fix $\kappa\le c\log n$ and set $L:=2\kappa$.

\[
T \;=\; O\!\big(\kappa\log N\big)
\]
such that for every $S\in\binom{[N]}{\kappa}$ some $h_t$ is injective on $S$.

label: lem:private-literal-unique
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_text: For each witness block B_i used in the NP construction, there exists a designated literal pad variable ell _i such that: ell _i occurs in the NP polynomial Q_ Φ_n only inside the unique local gadget factor associated with B_i , and no other local gadget contains ell _i .
title: Private literal uniqueness

label: lem:private-linear-unique
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{lem:private-linear-unique}
For each witness block $B_i$, the local gadget factor has the form
\[
G_i(\ell_i, y_i) = \ell_i + H_i(y_i),
\]
where $y_i$ are the remaining variables of the block and $H_i$ does not contain $\ell_i$.
In particular, $[\ell_i]G_i=1$ and no other monomial of $G_i$ has the same support as $\ell_i$.
statement_text: For each witness block B_i , the local gadget factor has the form \[ G_i(ell _i, y_i) = ell _i + H_i(y_i), \] where y_i are the remaining variables of the block and H_i does not contain ell _i . In particular, [ell _i]G_i=1 and no other monomial of G_i has the same support as ell _i .
title: Private literal appears linearly and uniquely

label: lem:pi-plus-unit

statement_text: There is a fixed, block-local invertible linear change of variables Π^+ (chosen once for the compiler/gadget family) such that, after applying Π^+ to each witness block, the designated private literal ell _i appears with coefficient +1 in the corresponding local gadget polynomial, and no other monomial in that local gadget shares the same support as the private monomial used in the identity-minor construction.

label: lem:no-cross-interference
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{lem:no-cross-interference}
Let $S\neq S'$ be two $\kappa$-sets of blocks. Let $x_{\beta(S)}$ be the private column monomial
constructed from the private literals of $S$. Then the coefficient of $x_{\beta(S)}$ in the
row polynomial corresponding to $(S',u')$ is zero:
\[
[x_{\beta(S)}]\big(u'\cdot \partial_{S'} Q_{\Phi_n}\big)=0.
\]
statement_text: Let S ≠ S' be two κ -sets of blocks. Let x_ β(S) be the private column monomial constructed from the private literals of S . Then the coefficient of x_ β(S) in the row polynomial corresponding to (S',u') is zero: \[ [x_ β(S) ] (u' · partial _ S' Q_ Φ_n )=0. \]

label: lem:identity-minor-k-injective
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{lem:identity-minor-k-injective}
Let $Q^{\times}_\Phi$ be the coupled NP-side SoS polynomial (Definition~\ref{def:Qphi-times}) with clause/witness block layout and block-local,
radius-$1$ gadgets. Fix $\kappa=\Theta(\log n)$ and let $\mathcal H$ be a $\kappa$-injective family as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:k-injective-family} with $L=2\kappa$. Then there exists a set $\mathcal I$ of
row/column indices of size
\[
|\mathcal I| \;\ge\; \binom{N'}{\kappa}
\quad\text{for some}\quad N'=\Theta(N),
\]
such that the submatrix of $M_{\kappa,\ell}(Q^{\times}_\Phi)$ indexed by $\mathcal I\times\mathcal I$ is the identity.
Consequently,
\(
\Gamma_{\kappa,\ell}(Q^{\times}_\Phi)\;\ge\;\binom{N'}{\kappa}\;=\;n^{\Theta(\log n)}.
\)
statement_text: Let Q^ × _Φ be the coupled NP-side SoS polynomial (Definition ) with clause/witness block layout and block-local, radius- 1 gadgets. Fix κ=Θ( log n) and let H be a κ -injective family as in Lemma with L=2κ . Then there exists a set I of row/column indices of size \[ |I| ≥ binom N' κ quad for some quad N'=Θ(N), \] such that the submatrix of M_ κ,ell (Q^ × _Φ) indexed by I × I is the identity. Consequently, \( Γ_ κ,ell (Q^ × _Φ) ≥ binom N' κ = n^ Θ( log n) . \)
title: Identity minor from κ -injective coloring

label: lem:splitter-appg-duplicate
paper_title: Toward P vs NP: An Observer-Theoretic Separation via SPDP Rank and a ZFC-Equivalent Foundation within the N-Frame Model
statement_tex:
\label{lem:splitter-appg-duplicate}
There exist absolute constants $c_0,c_1>0$ and, for all $N,\kappa$ with $1\le \kappa\le c_0\log N$, a family
$\mathcal{F}\subseteq {[N] \choose O(\kappa)}$ of size $\le N^{c_1}$ such that for every $\kappa$-set $S\subseteq [N]$
there is $F\in\mathcal{F}$ with $|S\cap F|=1$.
Moreover, given $S$ and $F$ with $|S\cap F|=1$, there is a monomial $x^\beta$ using only variables in $F$
such that $x^\beta$ appears in the $(S,u)$-row of $M_{\kappa,0}(Q_{\Phi_n})$ with nonzero coefficient, while for
any $S'\neq S$ in ${{[N]}\choose \kappa}$ the $(S',u')$-row has zero coefficient on $x^\beta$.
statement_text: There exist absolute constants c_0,c_1>0 and, for all N,κ with 1 ≤ κ ≤ c_0 log N , a family F ⊆ [N] choose O(κ) of size ≤ N^ c_1 such that for every κ -set S ⊆ [N] there is F ∈ F with |S ∩ F|=1 . Moreover, given S and F with |S ∩ F|=1 , there is a monomial x^β using only variables in F such that x^β appears in the (S,u) -row of M_ κ,0 (Q_ Φ_n ) with nonzero coefficient, while for any S' ≠ S in [N] choose κ the (S',u') -row has zero coefficient on x^β .

label: thm:np-identity-minor-formal-appg

\label{thm:np-identity-minor-formal-appg}
For $\kappa = \Theta(\log n)$ and $N=\Theta(n)$, there exists a column subfamily $\mathcal{C}$ and a row subfamily
$\mathcal{R}=\big\{(S,1): S\in {[N]\choose \kappa}\big\}$ such that the submatrix
$M_{\kappa,0}(Q_{\Phi_n})[\mathcal{R},\mathcal{C}]$ is the identity matrix of size $\binom{N}{\kappa}$.

\]

statement_tex:
\label{thm:non-algebrizing-collapse}
Fix $(\kappa,\ell)=\Theta(\log n)$ and a fixed block partition $\mathcal{B}$.
There exists an algebraic oracle $A$ such that the following fails relative to $A$:

\smallskip
\centerline{\emph{(Compiled SPDP collapse)$^{A}$: every $M\in\mathrm{P}^{A}$ compiles to
$\Gamma^{\mathcal{B}}_{\kappa,\ell}(p_{M,n})\le n^{O(1)}$.}}

\smallskip
In particular, any separation route whose P-side hinge is the compiled SPDP collapse lemma
is \emph{not} an algebrizing proof technique.

$p^t:=p$ \quad where $p$ is an atom
\item 
$1^t:=1$ \qquad $0^t:=D$ \qquad $\top^t:=\top$ \qquad $\bot^t:=\bot$
\item 
$(A \circ B)^t:=A^t \circ B^t$  for $\circ \in \{\wedge, \vee, *\}$
\item 
$(A \to B)^t:=(A^t \to B^t) \wedge (B^s \to A^s)$
\item 
$(!A)^t:=!A^t$ 
\end{itemize}

\noindent $\circ$ Translation $(\cdot)^s$:
\begin{itemize}
\item 

$p^s:= N$ \quad where $p$ is an atom 
\item 
$1^s:= D$ \qquad $0^s:= 1$ \qquad $\top^s:= \bot$ \qquad $\bot^s:= \top$ 
\item 
$(A \wedge B)^s:= A^s \vee B^s$ \qquad $(A \vee B)^s:= A^s \wedge B^s$
\item
$(A * B)^s:= (A^t \to B^s) \wedge (B^t \to A^s)$ 
\item 
$(A \to B)^s:= A^t \st B^s$ \qquad $(!A)^s:= !A^t \to D$
\end{itemize}
For any $\mathcal{L} \in \{\mathcal{L}_u, \mathcal{L}_b\}$, if $N, D \in \mathcal{L}$, the translations can be defined analogously over $\mathcal{L}$ by replacing $\mathcal{L}_!$ with $\mathcal{L}$ and restricting to formulas in $\mathcal{L}$.
statement_text: Fix formulas D,N ∈ L _! and define the translation functions ( · )^t: L _! → L _! and ( · )^s: L _! → L _! simultaneously and inductively as follows: ∘ Translation ( · )^t : p^t:=p quad where p is an atom 1^t:=1 qquad 0^t:=D qquad top ^t:=top qquad bot ^t:=bot (A ∘ B)^t:=A^t ∘ B^t for ∘ ∈ {wedge , vee , *} (A → B)^t:=(A^t → B^t) wedge (B^s → A^s) (!A)^t:=!A^t ∘ Translation ( · )^s : p^s:= N quad where p is an atom 1^s:= D qquad 0^s:= 1 qquad top ^s:= bot qquad bot ^s:= top (A wedge B)^s:= A^s vee B^s qquad (A vee B)^s:= A^s wedge B^s (A * B)^s:= (A^t → B^s) wedge (B^t → A^s) (A → B)^s:= A^t * B^s qquad (!A)^s:= !A^t → D For any L ∈ { L _u, L _b} , if N, D ∈ L , the translations can be defined analogously over L by replacing L _! with L and restricting to formulas in L .
title: Chu's translation

label: Lem: iGD
paper_title: Proof Complexity of Linear Logics
statement_tex:
\label{Lem: iGD}
Let $\calL \in \{\calL_u, \calL_b, \calL_!\}$, let $A$ be an $\calL$-formula and $L \in \{\CFL, \allowbreak \MALL, \CLL\}$ with the calculus $G$. The following sequents have $iG_D$-proofs with $O(|A|)$ many lines:
\[
A^t, A^s \Rightarrow D \qquad (\neg A)^t \Leftrightarrow A^s \qquad (\neg A)^s \Leftrightarrow A^t.
\]
statement_text: Let L ∈ { L _u, L _b, L _!} , let A be an L -formula and L ∈ { CFL_e , allowbreak MALL , LL } with the calculus G . The following sequents have iG_D -proofs with O(|A|) many lines: \[ A^t, A^s ⇒ D qquad ( ¬ A)^t ⟺ A^s qquad ( ¬ A)^s ⟺ A^t. \]

label: thm: CFLe to FL_e
paper_title: Proof Complexity of Linear Logics
statement_tex:
{theorem}{ThmCFLeToFLe} \label{thm: CFLe to FL_e}
Let $L \in \{\CFL, \MALL, \CLL\}$ with the sequent calculus $G$ and Frege system $L$-$\F$. Then, for any $L$-$\F$ proof $\pi$ of $A$, there exists an $iG_D$-proof $\sigma$ of $(\, \Rightarrow A^t)$ such that $l(\sigma) \leq O(|\pi|)$. In case $D=\bot$, the claim also holds for any $L \in \{\AMALL, \ALL\}$.
statement_text: theorem ThmCFLeToFLe Let L ∈ { CFL_e , MALL , LL } with the sequent calculus G and Frege system L - F . Then, for any L - F proof π of A , there exists an iG_D -proof σ of ( ⇒ A^t) such that l(σ) ≤ O(|π|) . In case D=bot , the claim also holds for any L ∈ { MALL_ w , LLW } .

label: Def: Conservative formulas
paper_title: Proof Complexity of Linear Logics
statement_text: Define the following sets of L _! -formulas simultaneously: ( Fully conservative ) B:= p mid 1 mid top mid B wedge B mid B vee B mid C → B , where p is an atom and C is conservative ( Conservative ) C := bot mid B mid C wedge C mid C vee C mid C * C mid !C , where B is fully conservative. A formula in the languages L _b is called fully conservative or conservative if it is so in the extended language L _! .

label: Exam: conservative
paper_title: Proof Complexity of Linear Logics
statement_tex:
\label{Exam: conservative}
The formulas $p \wedge q$, $p \vee q$, and $p \to q$, where $p$ and $q$ are atoms, are all fully conservative, while $p * q$ and $!p$ are conservative but not fully conservative. Note that $(p * q) \to r$ and $!p \to r$ are fully conservative. Moreover, $0$ is neither conservative nor fully conservative and $\bot$ is conservative but not fully conservative.
statement_text: The formulas p wedge q , p vee q , and p → q , where p and q are atoms, are all fully conservative, while p * q and !p are conservative but not fully conservative. Note that (p * q) → r and !p → r are fully conservative. Moreover, 0 is neither conservative nor fully conservative and bot is conservative but not fully conservative.

label: lem: basic conservative
paper_title: Proof Complexity of Linear Logics
statement_tex:
\label{lem: basic conservative}
Fix $D=N=\bot$ and let $B$ be a fully conservative and $C$ be a conservative $\calL_b$-formula. Then, there are $\pi_1$, $\pi_2$, $\sigma$, $\tau_1$, and $\tau_2$ such that:
\begin{itemize}
    \item 
$\BIMALL \vdash^{\pi_1} B^t \Rightarrow B$ and $\BIMALL \vdash^{\pi_2} B \Rightarrow B^t$,
\item 
$\BIMALL \vdash^{\sigma} B^s \Rightarrow \bot$,
\item 
$\BIMALL \vdash^{\tau_1} C^t \Rightarrow C$ and $\BIMALL \vdash^{\tau_2} C \Rightarrow C^t$, and
\end{itemize}
$l(\pi_i) \leq O(|B|^2)$, $ l(\sigma) \leq O(|B|)$, and $l(\tau_i) \leq O(|C|^2)$, for any $i \in \{1, 2\}$.
If $B$ and $C$ are $\calL_!$-formulas, then the same results hold when replacing $\BIMALL$ by $\BILL$.
statement_text: Fix D=N=bot and let B be a fully conservative and C be a conservative L _b -formula. Then, there are π_1 , π_2 , σ , τ_1 , and τ_2 such that: IMALL vdash ^ π_1 B^t ⇒ B and IMALL vdash ^ π_2 B ⇒ B^t , IMALL vdash ^ σ B^s ⇒ bot , IMALL vdash ^ τ_1 C^t ⇒ C and IMALL vdash ^ τ_2 C ⇒ C^t , and l(π_i) ≤ O(|B|^2) , l(σ) ≤ O(|B|) , and l(τ_i) ≤ O(|C|^2) , for any i ∈ {1, 2} . If B and C are L _! -formulas, then the same results hold when replacing IMALL by ILL .

label: Thm: Conservativity
paper_title: Proof Complexity of Linear Logics
statement_tex:
\label{Thm: Conservativity}

Let $G \in \{\BMALL, \BAMALL, \BCLL, \BALL\}$. Then, for any conservative formula $A$ and any $G$-proof $\pi$ of $A$ there is an $iG$-proof $\sigma$ of $A$ such that $l(\sigma) \leq |\pi|^{O(1)}$.
statement_text: Let G ∈ { MALL , MALL_ w , LL , LLW } . Then, for any conservative formula A and any G -proof π of A there is an iG -proof σ of A such that l(σ) ≤ |π|^ O(1) .

label: Thm: main
paper_title: Proof Complexity of Linear Logics
statement_tex:
\label{Thm: main}
The $\BFL$-provable sequents $(\Rightarrow \Theta^{*}_n)$ have $\LKu$-proofs of size $n^{O(1)}$, while any of their $\BALL$-proofs has size at least $2^{n^{\Omega(1)}}$. The same result holds when replacing $\LKu$ and $\BALL$ with the Frege systems for $\CPC$ and $\ALL$, respectively.
statement_text: The FL_e -provable sequents ( ⇒ Θ^ * _n) have LK_u -proofs of size n^ O(1) , while any of their LLW -proofs has size at least 2^ n^ Ω(1) . The same result holds when replacing LK_u and LLW with the Frege systems for CPC and LLW , respectively.

label: Def: Lnn
paper_title: Proof Complexity of Linear Logics
statement_tex:
\label{Def: Lnn}
    An $\mathcal{L}_p$-formula $F$ is in \emph{negation normal form} (\emph{nnf}, in short), if it is defined by the following grammar:
\[
F:= p \mid \neg p \mid F_1 \wedge F_2 \mid F_1 \vee F_2
\]
Similarly, an $\calL_u$-formula $F$ is in \emph{$*$-negation normal form} (\emph{$*$-nnf}, in short), if it is defined by the grammar:
\[
F:= p \mid \neg p \mid F_1 \wedge F_2 \mid F_1 \vee F_2 \mid  F_1 \st F_2
\]
We write $\calL_{nn}$ and $\calL^*_{nn}$ for the sets of nnf- and $*$-nnf-formulas.
statement_text: An L _p -formula F is in negation normal form ( nnf , in short), if it is defined by the following grammar: \[ F:= p mid ¬ p mid F_1 wedge F_2 mid F_1 vee F_2 \] Similarly, an L _u -formula F is in * -negation normal form ( * -nnf , in short), if it is defined by the grammar: \[ F:= p mid ¬ p mid F_1 wedge F_2 mid F_1 vee F_2 mid F_1 * F_2 \] We write L _ nn and L ^*_ nn for the sets of nnf- and * -nnf-formulas.

label: Def: Calculus G
paper_title: Proof Complexity of Linear Logics
statement_text: Define the single-conclusion sequent calculus G over L _u as FL_e plus the following initial sequents: ⇒ p vee ¬ p qquad p ⇒ 1 qquad ¬ p ⇒ 1 qquad 0 ⇒ p qquad 0 ⇒ ¬ p qquad 0 ⇒ 0*0 , where p is an atom. Note that these initial sequents are not meant to be used as axioms and hence using their substitutions are not allowed in G . Moreover, G includes the cut rule.

label: lem: law of excluded middle
paper_title: Proof Complexity of Linear Logics
statement_tex:
\label{lem: law of excluded middle}
For any $A \in \calL^*_{nn}$, the following sequents have tree-like $G$-proofs of size $|A|^{O(1)}$:
\[
A \Rightarrow 1 \qquad 0 \Rightarrow A \qquad \Rightarrow A \vee \neg A \qquad A \Rightarrow A * A.
\]
statement_text: For any A ∈ L ^*_ nn , the following sequents have tree-like G -proofs of size |A|^ O(1) : \[ A ⇒ 1 qquad 0 ⇒ A qquad ⇒ A vee ¬ A qquad A ⇒ A * A. \]

label: Def: Calculus LKnn
paper_title: Proof Complexity of Linear Logics
statement_text: Define LK_ nn over L _ nn as the single-conclusion sequent calculus consisting of the following axioms: p ⇒ p qquad ¬ p ⇒ ¬ p qquad p, ¬ p ⇒ qquad ⇒ p vee ¬ p along with the structural rules (including cut), conjunction and disjunction rules of LJ .

label: Lem: LKnn to G
paper_title: Proof Complexity of Linear Logics
statement_tex:
\label{Lem: LKnn to G}
Let $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$ be multisets of nnf-formulas, where $\Delta$ contains at most one formula. For any tree-like $\LKnn$-proof $\pi$ of $\Gamma \Rightarrow \Delta$, there is a tree-like $G$-proof $\sigma_\pi$ of $\Gamma \Rightarrow \Delta$ such that $|\sigma_\pi| \leq |\pi|^{O(1)}$.
statement_text: Let Γ and Δ be multisets of nnf-formulas, where Δ contains at most one formula. For any tree-like LK_ nn -proof π of Γ ⇒ Δ , there is a tree-like G -proof σ_π of Γ ⇒ Δ such that |σ_π| ≤ |π|^ O(1) .

label: Cor: LK to G
paper_title: Proof Complexity of Linear Logics
statement_tex:
\label{Cor: LK to G}
Let $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$ be multisets of nnf-formulas, where $\Delta$ contains at most one formula. For any tree-like $\LK$-proof $\pi$ of $\Gamma \Rightarrow \Delta$, there exists a tree-like $G$-proof $\sigma_\pi$ of $\Gamma \Rightarrow \Delta$ such that $|\sigma_\pi| \leq |\pi|^{O(1)}$.
statement_text: Let Γ and Δ be multisets of nnf-formulas, where Δ contains at most one formula. For any tree-like LK -proof π of Γ ⇒ Δ , there exists a tree-like G -proof σ_π of Γ ⇒ Δ such that |σ_π| ≤ |π|^ O(1) .

label: Def: forgetful
paper_title: Proof Complexity of Linear Logics
statement_text: Define the forgetful function ( · )^f: L _! → L _p as: p^f:=p qquad 0^f:= bot qquad 1^f:= top qquad (A * B)^f:= A^f wedge B^f (A ∘ B)^f:= A^f ∘ B^f for ∘ ∈ {wedge , vee , → } qquad (!A)^f:=A^f Define Γ^f:= {A^f mid A ∈ Γ} and S^f:= Γ^f ⇒ Δ^f , for any multisets Γ and Δ and any sequent S of the form Γ ⇒ Δ .

label: Thm: G to FLe
paper_title: Proof Complexity of Linear Logics
statement_tex:
\label{Thm: G to FLe}
Let $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$ be multisets of $\calL_u$-formulas, where $\Delta$ contains at most one formula. For any tree-like $G$-proof $\pi$ of $\Gamma \Rightarrow \Delta$, there exists a multiset $\Sigma_{\pi}$ of single-variable $\calL_u$-formulas and an $\BFL$-proof $\sigma_\pi$ of $\Sigma_\pi, \Gamma \Rightarrow \Delta$, such that $|\Sigma_\pi| \leq O(|\pi|)$, $|\sigma_\pi| \leq O(|\pi|^3)$, and $\LK \vdash \, \Rightarrow \bigwedge \Sigma_\pi^f$.
statement_text: Let Γ and Δ be multisets of L _u -formulas, where Δ contains at most one formula. For any tree-like G -proof π of Γ ⇒ Δ , there exists a multiset Σ_ π of single-variable L _u -formulas and an FL_e -proof σ_π of Σ_π, Γ ⇒ Δ , such that |Σ_π| ≤ O(|π|) , |σ_π| ≤ O(|π|^3) , and LK vdash ⇒ wedge Σ_π^f .
title: Feasible Deduction Theorem

label: Cor: LK to FLe
paper_title: Proof Complexity of Linear Logics
statement_tex:
\label{Cor: LK to FLe}
There exist a sequence $\{\Sigma_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ of multisets of single-variable $\calL_u$-formulas and a sequence $\{\sigma_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ such that each $\sigma_n$ is an $\BFL$-proof for
\[
\Sigma_{n},\; Clique_n(\bar{p}, \bar{r}) \Rightarrow \overline{Color}_n(\bar{p}, \bar{s}),
\]
$|\Sigma_{n}|,|\sigma_{n}| \leq n^{O(1)}$ and $\LK \vdash \, \Rightarrow \bigwedge \Sigma_{n}^f$.
statement_text: There exist a sequence {Σ_n}_ n=1 ^ ∞ of multisets of single-variable L _u -formulas and a sequence {σ_n}_ n=1 ^ ∞ such that each σ_n is an FL_e -proof for \[ Σ_ n , Clique_n(bar p , bar r ) ⇒ overline Color _n(bar p , bar s ), \] |Σ_ n |,|σ_ n | ≤ n^ O(1) and LK vdash ⇒ wedge Σ_ n ^f .

label: MainCutFree
paper_title: Proof Complexity of Linear Logics
statement_tex:
\label{MainCutFree}
The sequents
\[
S_n := Clique_n(\bar{p}, \bar{r}),\; \Pi_n \;\Rightarrow\; \bigast \Sigma_n^{\bar{p}, \bar{s}} \to \overline{Color}_n(\bar{p}, \bar{s})
\]
have $\BFL$-proofs of size $n^{O(1)}$, but any $\mathbf{LK^-_!}$-proof of $S_n$ has size $2^{n^{\Omega(1)}}$.
statement_text: The sequents \[ S_n := Clique_n(bar p , bar r ), Π_n ⇒ mathop scalebox 1.5 raisebox -0.2ex ast Σ_n^ bar p , bar s → overline Color _n(bar p , bar s ) \] have FL_e -proofs of size n^ O(1) , but any LK^-_! -proof of S_n has size 2^ n^ Ω(1) .

label: Cor: cut free
paper_title: Proof Complexity of Linear Logics
statement_tex:
\label{Cor: cut free}
There is an exponential speed-up between any of the sequent calculi $\BFL$, $\BFLc$, $\BFLw$, $\LJ$, $\BCFL$, $\BCFLc$, $\BCFLw$, $\LK$, $\BIMALL$, $\BAIMALL$, $\BRIMALL$, $\BILL$, $\BCLL$, $\BELL$, $\BALL$, $\BRLL$   and their cut-free versions.
statement_text: There is an exponential speed-up between any of the sequent calculi FL_e , FL_ ec , FL_ ew , LJ , CFL_e , CFL_ ec , CFL_ ew , LK , IMALL , IMALL_ w , IMALL_c , ILL , LL , ELL , LLW , LLC and their cut-free versions.

label: defvc
paper_title: Hardness and Tractability of T_{h+1}-Free Edge Deletion
statement_tex:
\label{defvc}
A set $S \subseteq V(G)$ is a \emph{vertex cover} of $G$ if  every edge in $E(G)$ has at least one  endpoint in $S$. The \emph{size} of a smallest vertex cover of  $G$ is the \emph{vertex cover number} of $G$.
statement_text: A set S ⊆ V(G) is a vertex cover of G if every edge in E(G) has at least one endpoint in S . The size of a smallest vertex cover of G is the vertex cover number of G .

label: deffvs
paper_title: Hardness and Tractability of T_{h+1}-Free Edge Deletion
statement_tex:
\label{deffvs}
 A \emph{feedback vertex set}  of a graph  $G$ is a set of vertices whose removal turns $G$ into a forest. The minimum size of a feedback vertex set in $G$ is the \emph{ feedback vertex set number} of $G$.
statement_text: A feedback vertex set of a graph G is a set of vertices whose removal turns G into a forest. The minimum size of a feedback vertex set in G is the feedback vertex set number of G .

label: deftd
paper_title: Hardness and Tractability of T_{h+1}-Free Edge Deletion
statement_tex:
\label{deftd}~\cite{bib12}
         The \emph{ treedepth} of a graph $G$ is the minimum height of a rooted forest $Y$ whose closure contains the graph $G$ as a subgraph. It is denoted by $td(G)$.
statement_text: The treedepth of a graph G is the minimum height of a rooted forest Y whose closure contains the graph G as a subgraph. It is denoted by td(G) .

paper_title: Hardness and Tractability of T_{h+1}-Free Edge Deletion
statement_tex:
~\cite{bib13}
An edge $uv\in E(G)$ is a \emph{twin edge} of $G$ if $N[u]=N[v]$.
statement_text: An edge uv ∈ E(G) is a twin edge of G if N[u]=N[v] .

label: deftc
paper_title: Hardness and Tractability of T_{h+1}-Free Edge Deletion
statement_text: A set X ⊆ V(G) is a twin-cover of G if every edge in G is either twin edge or incident to a vertex in X . The twin-cover number of G , denoted as tc(G) , is the minimum possible size of a twin-cover of G .

label: defnd
paper_title: Hardness and Tractability of T_{h+1}-Free Edge Deletion
statement_tex:
~\cite{Lampis}\label{defnd}
A graph  $G$
 has \emph{neighborhood diversity} at most $d$, if there exists a partition of $V(G)$
 into at most $d$
 sets (we call these sets {\it type classes}) such that all the vertices in each set have the same neighborhood type.
statement_text: A graph G has neighborhood diversity at most d , if there exists a partition of V(G) into at most d sets (we call these sets it type classes ) such that all the vertices in each set have the same neighborhood type.

paper_title: Hardness and Tractability of T_{h+1}-Free Edge Deletion
statement_tex:
A {\it tree decomposition} of a 
graph~$G=(V,E)$  is a tree $T$ together with a 
collection of subsets $X_t$ (called \emph{bags}) of $V$ labeled by the nodes $t$ of $T$ such that 
$\bigcup_{t\in T}X_t=V $ and (1) and (2) below hold:
\begin{enumerate}
			\item For every edge $uv \in E(G)$, there  is some $t$ such that $\{u,v\}\subseteq X_t$.
			\item  (Interpolation Property) If $t$ is a node on the unique path in $T$ from $t_1$ to $t_2$, then 
			$X_{t_1}\cap X_{t_2}\subseteq X_t$.
		\end{enumerate}
statement_text: A it tree decomposition of a graph G=(V,E) is a tree T together with a collection of subsets X_t (called bags ) of V labeled by the nodes t of T such that cup_ t ∈ T X_t=V and (1) and (2) below hold: For every edge uv ∈ E(G) , there is some t such that {u,v} ⊆ X_t . (Interpolation Property) If t is a node on the unique path in T from t_1 to t_2 , then X_ t_1 ∩ X_ t_2 ⊆ X_t .
title: Robertson and Seymour

label: deftw
paper_title: Hardness and Tractability of T_{h+1}-Free Edge Deletion
statement_tex:
\label{deftw}~\cite{Neil} The {\it width} of a tree decomposition is
the maximum value of $|X_t|-1 $ taken over all the nodes $t$ of the tree $T$ of the decomposition.
The \emph{treewidth} $tw(G)$ of a graph $G$  is the  minimum width among all possible tree decompositions of $G$.
statement_text: The it width of a tree decomposition is the maximum value of |X_t|-1 taken over all the nodes t of the tree T of the decomposition. The treewidth tw(G) of a graph G is the minimum width among all possible tree decompositions of G .

label: defpw
paper_title: Hardness and Tractability of T_{h+1}-Free Edge Deletion
statement_text: If the tree T of a tree decomposition is a path, then we say that the tree decomposition is a it path decomposition . The pathwidth pw(G) of a graph G is the minimum width among all possible path decompositions of G .

label: cvd def
paper_title: Hardness and Tractability of T_{h+1}-Free Edge Deletion
statement_tex:
\label{cvd def}
   The \emph{cluster vertex deletion number} of a graph is the minimum number of its vertices whose deletion results in a disjoint union of complete graphs.
statement_text: The cluster vertex deletion number of a graph is the minimum number of its vertices whose deletion results in a disjoint union of complete graphs.

label: thm:distF
paper_title: Hardness and Tractability of T_{h+1}-Free Edge Deletion
statement_tex:
\label{thm:distF}
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be any graph class that contains a connected graph on $s$ vertices
for every $s\in\mathbb{N}$.
Then \textsc{$\mathcal{T}_{h+1}$-Free Edge Deletion} is \emph{W[1]-hard} when parameterized by
the vertex deletion distance of the input graph to $\mathcal{F}$.
statement_text: Let F be any graph class that contains a connected graph on s vertices for every s ∈ N . Then sc T _ h+1 -Free Edge Deletion is W[1]-hard when parameterized by the vertex deletion distance of the input graph to F .

label: cor:masterF
paper_title: Hardness and Tractability of T_{h+1}-Free Edge Deletion
statement_text: sc T _ h+1 -Free Edge Deletion is W[1]-hard when parameterized by each of the following parameters: the size of a vertex set whose deletion turns the graph into a disjoint union of cliques; the size of a vertex set whose deletion turns the graph into a disjoint union of paths; the size of a vertex set whose deletion turns the graph into a disjoint union of stars. Moreover, by choosing all gadgets A_i and H_j to be cliques in the reduction, we obtain that sc T _ h+1 -Free Edge Deletion is W[1]-hard parameterized by the twin cover number.

paper_title: Hardness and Tractability of T_{h+1}-Free Edge Deletion
statement_tex: $\mathcal{T}_{h+1}$-\textnormal{\textsc{Free Edge Deletion}}  is W[1]-hard parameterized by the treedepth, cluster vertex deletion number or modular width of the input graph.
statement_text: T _ h+1 -normal sc Free Edge Deletion is W[1]-hard parameterized by the treedepth, cluster vertex deletion number or modular width of the input graph.

label: lem1
paper_title: Hardness and Tractability of T_{h+1}-Free Edge Deletion
statement_tex:
\label{lem1}
     If $|C'| = qh+r$ where $q,r \in \mathbb{N }$ and $0 \leq r <h$, then in the graph $G \setminus F$, the set $C'$ induces a disjoint union of $q$ cliques of size $h$ and one clique of size $r$.
statement_text: If |C'| = qh+r where q,r ∈ N and 0 ≤ r <h , then in the graph G \ F , the set C' induces a disjoint union of q cliques of size h and one clique of size r .

paper_title: Hardness and Tractability of T_{h+1}-Free Edge Deletion
statement_tex: $\mathcal{T}_{h+1}$-\textnormal{\textsc{Free Edge Deletion}}  can be solved in $\mathcal{O}\!\left((2^{\ell}\ell h^{2})^{\mathcal{O}(2^{\ell}\ell h)} \cdot (n+m)\right)$ time.
statement_text: T _ h+1 -normal sc Free Edge Deletion can be solved in O ((2^ ell ell h^ 2 )^ O (2^ ell ell h) · (n+m) ) time.

label: thm:vdclique_iqp
paper_title: Hardness and Tractability of T_{h+1}-Free Edge Deletion
statement_text: sc T _ h+1 -Free Edge Deletion is fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the size ell of a vertex deletion set to a clique.

label: claim:parts
paper_title: Hardness and Tractability of T_{h+1}-Free Edge Deletion
statement_text: There exists an optimal solution F^star such that in H^star := G \ F^star , the vertex set V(G) can be partitioned into parts Q_1, ... ,Q_p satisfying: |Q_r| ≤ h for every r ∈ [p] , and all but at most one part satisfy |Q_r| ≥ lceil h/2rceil .

paper_title: Hardness and Tractability of T_{h+1}-Free Edge Deletion
statement_tex: In Claim~\ref{claim:parts}, we may assume the number of parts satisfies $$p \le f(\ell) := 2^{\ell+1}(\ell+1)+2\ell+1$$.
statement_text: In Claim , we may assume the number of parts satisfies p ≤ f(ell ) := 2^ ell +1 (ell +1)+2ell +1 .

paper_title: Hardness and Tractability of T_{h+1}-Free Edge Deletion
statement_tex:
For a fixed guess $(p,s)$, the optimum value of the IQP equals the minimum size of an
edge set $F$ such that $G\setminus F$ has a partition into $p$ parts satisfying

paper_title: On Condensation of Block Sensitivity, Certificate Complexity and the $\mathsf{AND}$ (and $\mathsf{OR}$) Decision Tree Complexity
statement_tex: An \textbf{$\fand$-Decision Tree} is a deterministic query model that generalizes the classical decision tree. While a classical tree queries individual input bits $x_i\in \{0, 1\}$, each internal node in an $\mathsf{AND}$-decision tree queries a conjunction of a subset of input bits. Formally, a node $v$ computes a function $f_v(x) = \bigwedge\limits_{i\in S_v} x_i$ for some $S_v\subseteq [n]$, the decision to which child to choose is based on the binary outcome of this query.

While a classical tree queries individual input bits x_i ∈ {0, 1} , each internal node in an AND -decision tree queries a conjunction of a subset of input bits. Formally, a node v computes a function f_v(x) = wedge _ i ∈ S_v x_i for some S_v ⊆ [n] , the decision to which child to choose is based on the binary outcome of this query.

statement_tex:
An {\em $\eps$-perfect equilibrium} is a fully-mixed profile $\vlambda$ such that every player is playing an $\eps$-perfect best response. A {\em perfect equilibrium} is a limit point of $\eps$-perfect equilibria as $\eps \to 0$. Formally, $\vlambda^*$ is a perfect equilibrium if there are infinite sequences $\{ \vlambda^{(t)}\}_{t=1}^\infty \to \vlambda^*$ and $\{ \eps^{(t)} \}_{t=1}^\infty \to 0$ such that $\vlambda^{(t)}$ is a $\eps^{(t)}$-perfect equilibrium for every $t$.

    We define {\em ($\eps$-)proper equilibria} identically, by replacing every instance of {\em perfect} with {\em proper}.

paper_title: Catalytic Tree Evaluation From Matching Vectors
statement_tex: A \textit{catalytic machine} $M$ is defined as a Turing machine in the usual sense---i.e.,~a read-only input tape, a write-only output tape, and a (space-bounded) read-write work tape---with an additional read-write tape known as the \textit{catalytic tape}. Unlike the ordinary work tape, the catalytic tape is initialized to hold an arbitrary string $\tau$, and $M$ has the restriction that for any initial setting of the catalytic tape, at the end of its computation the catalytic tape must be returned to the original state $\tau$.
statement_text: A it catalytic machine M is defined as a Turing machine in the usual sense---i.e., a read-only input tape, a write-only output tape, and a (space-bounded) read-write work tape---with an additional read-write tape known as the it catalytic tape . Unlike the ordinary work tape, the catalytic tape is initialized to hold an arbitrary string τ , and M has the restriction that for any initial setting of the catalytic tape, at the end of its computation the catalytic tape must be returned to the original state τ .

label: thm:TEPonelevel

statement_tex:
\label{thm:TEPonelevel}
    Let $m = p_1p_2\ldots p_t$ be a product of $t$ distinct odd primes that are given as input.
    Suppose there exists an $O(\ell)$-space uniform
    matching vector family $\{\uv_x, \vecv_x \in \Z_m^d: x \in \zo^\ell\}$ of size $2^\ell$ over $\Z_m^d$.
    Additionally, let $\left\{\wv_s: s \in \zo^\ell\right\}$ be any $O(\ell)$-space uniform collection of vectors in $\Z_m^{d}$.
    Suppose our algorithm is given the following resources:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item global space 
        comprising three 
        registers $\xv, \yv,\zv \in \Z_m^d$;
        \item the truth table of a function $f: \zo^\ell \times \zo^\ell \to \zo^\ell$ on the input tape; and
        \item an oracle $\calO$ that takes as input a scalar $\gamma \in \Z_m$ and bits $\ctrl, \sigma \in \zo$ in local space and updates the registers as follows.
        In the below, $a, b \in \zo^\ell$ are some bitstrings.
        \begin{itemize}
            \item if $\sigma = 0$, let $\Delta$ denote $\uv_a$ if $\mathsf{ctrl} = 0$ and $\vecv_a$ otherwise.
            The oracle will update $\xv \gets \xv + \gamma \Delta$ and leave all other registers unchanged.
            (Here, by $\xv$ we mean the first of the three catalytic registers, and $\yv$ refers to the second catalytic register.)

            \item if $\sigma = 1$, let $\Delta$ denote $\uv_b$ if $\mathsf{ctrl} = 0$ and $\vecv_b$ otherwise.
            The oracle will update $\yv \gets \yv + \gamma \Delta$ and leave all other registers unchanged.
        \end{itemize}
    \end{itemize}
    Then, there exists an algorithm that takes as input a scalar $\gamma \in \Z_m$ in local space and updates $\zv \gets \zv + \gamma \wv_{f(a, b)}$ (while leaving the $\xv$ and $\yv$ registers unchanged). Moreover, the algorithm uses $O(\ell + \log m + \log(d \cdot \log m))$ local space, and before making all oracle calls erases all but $O(\log m)$ bits of this space. The algorithm runs in time $\poly(2^{\ell+t} \cdot d \cdot \log m)$ and makes $2^{O(t)}$ queries to $\calO$.

paper_title: On the Complexity of Learning Nash Equilibria
statement_tex:
\label{def: nash convergence}
We describe several definitions, from most basic to most demanding.
    \begin{enumerate} [label=(\Alph*)]
\item \emph{Nash-convergence}: for all $x\in X_G$, $\lim_{t\rightarrow\infty} \phi(x,t)$ exists and is a Nash equilibrium. 

\item {\em Uniform Nash convergence} is (A) with a {\em Lyapunov function}, $L:X_G\mapsto [0,1],$ such that, if $x$ is not a Nash equilibrium, $L(\phi(x,t))< L(x)$ for all $t>0$.   

\item[(A$^+$)/(B$^+$)] is (A) or (B) with the addition of {\em Nash stationarity}, the requirement that all Nash equilibria are fixed points of the dynamic\footnote{Note that (A) already implies that every fixpoint is a Nash equilibrium --- Nash stationarity requires the converse.}.

\item Finally, and most strongly is what is called \emph{global Nash-convergence} in \cite{milionis_impossibility_2023}; this is (B$^+$) with the additional requirement that, if $N$ and $N'$ are Nash equilibria in the same connected component of the Nash equilibrium set, then $L(N)=L(N')$.
\end{enumerate}

statement_tex: Let $\phi$ be a dynamic. $\phi$ is \emph{Nash-convergent} if for every game $G$ and for all mixed strategy profiles $x\in X_G$, the limit $\lim_{t\to\infty} \phi(x,t)$ exists and is a Nash equilibrium of $G$. We say that $\phi$ is \emph{uniformly Nash-convergent} (globally Nash convergent in \cite{milionis_impossibility_2023}) if for all games there exists a Lyapunov function $L:X\to [0,1]$ where for all non-Nash $x$, $L(\phi(x,t)) < L(x)$ for all $t>0$.

label: def:weakening
paper_title: Separations above TFNP from Sherali-Adams Lower Bounds
statement_tex:
\phantomsection\label{def:weakening}
    Let $D$ be a DNF formula, a \emph{$\Sigma_2$-weakening} of $D$ is a collection of DNFs $\{D_i\}_{i \in [m]}$ such that $D \implies D_i$ for every $i \in [m]$. A $\Sigma_2$-weakening of a collection of DNFs is a union of $\Sigma_2$-weakening of those DNFs.
statement_text: phantomsection Let D be a DNF formula, a Σ_2 -weakening of D is a collection of DNFs {D_i}_ i ∈ [m] such that D ⇒ D_i for every i ∈ [m] . A Σ_2 -weakening of a collection of DNFs is a union of Σ_2 -weakening of those DNFs.

label: def:void
paper_title: Separations above TFNP from Sherali-Adams Lower Bounds
statement_tex:
\label{def:void} A total query search problem $R=(R_n)$, where $R_n \subseteq \{0,1\}^n \times {\cal O}_n$, belongs  to $\TF\Sigma_2^{dt}$ if for every $n$, $o \in {\cal O}_n$ and $x\in\{0,1\}^n$
\[ R_n(x,o) \iff \forall z \in \{0,1\}^{\ell}, V_{o,z}(x)=1,\]
where $\ell = \polylog(n)$ and for every $z \in \{0,1\}^{\ell}$, $V_{o,z}$ is a $\polylog(n)$-depth decision tree.
statement_text: A total query search problem R=(R_n) , where R_n ⊆ {0,1}^n × cal O _n , belongs to TF Σ_2^ dt if for every n , o ∈ cal O _n and x ∈ {0,1}^n \[ R_n(x,o) ⟺ ∀ z ∈ {0,1}^ ell , V_ o,z (x)=1,\] where ell = polylog (n) and for every z ∈ {0,1}^ ell , V_ o,z is a polylog (n) -depth decision tree.

label: def:many_one_red
paper_title: Separations above TFNP from Sherali-Adams Lower Bounds
statement_tex:
\label{def:many_one_red}
    For total query search problems $R \subseteq \{0,1\}^n \times {\cal O}_{n}, S \subseteq \{0,1\}^m \times {\cal O}_{m}'$, there is an \emph{$S$-formulation of $R$} if, for every $i \in [m]$ and $o \in {\cal O'}_m$, there are functions $f_i :\{0,1\}^n \rightarrow \{0,1\}$ and $g_o : \{0,1\}^n \rightarrow {\cal O}_n$ such that 
    \[ S(f(x),o) \implies R(x,g_o(x)),\]
      where $f(x) = (f_1(x) \ldots f_m(x))$. The \emph{depth} of the formulation is 
      \[d~:=~\max\big (\{ \depth(f_i) : i \in [m]\} \cup \{\depth(g_o): o \in {\cal O}_m'\} \big),\]
      where $\depth( f )$ denotes the minimum depth of any decision tree which computes $f$. The \emph{size} of the formulation is $m$, the number of input bits to $S$. The \emph{complexity} of the formulation is $\log m+d$.
      The \emph{complexity of reducing $R$ to $S$} is the minimum complexity of all possible $S$-formulations of $R$.

      We extend this definition to sequences in the natural way. If $S=(S_m)$ is a sequence and $R_n$ is a single search problem, then the complexity of reducing $R_n$ to $S$ is the minimum over $m$ of the complexity of reducing $R_n$ to $S_m$. For two sequences of search problems $S=(S_m)$ and $R=(R_n)$, the complexity of reducing $R$ to $S$ is the complexity of reducing $R_n$ to $S$, as a function of $n$. A reduction from $R$ to $S$ is efficient if its complexity is $\polylog(n)$; we denote this by $R \leq_{dt} S$.
statement_text: For total query search problems R ⊆ {0,1}^n × cal O _ n , S ⊆ {0,1}^m × cal O _ m ' , there is an S -formulation of R if, for every i ∈ [m] and o ∈ cal O' _m , there are functions f_i :{0,1}^n → {0,1} and g_o : {0,1}^n → cal O _n such that \[ S(f(x),o) ⇒ R(x,g_o(x)),\] where f(x) = (f_1(x) ... f_m(x)) . The depth of the formulation is \[d := max ({ depth (f_i) : i ∈ [m]} ∪ { depth (g_o): o ∈ cal O _m'} ),\] where depth ( f ) denotes the minimum depth of any decision tree which computes f . The size of the formulation is m , the number of input bits to S . The complexity of the formulation is log m+d . The complexity of reducing R to S is the minimum complexity of all possible S -formulations of R . We extend this definition to sequences in the natural way. If S=(S_m) is a sequence and R_n is a single search problem, then the complexity of reducing R_n to S is the minimum over m of the complexity of reducing R_n to S_m . For two sequences of search problems S=(S_m) and R=(R_n) , the complexity of reducing R to S is the complexity of reducing R_n to S , as a function of n . A reduction from R to S is efficient if its complexity is polylog (n) ; we denote this by R ≤ _ dt S .

label: def:uSAproofsyst
paper_title: Separations above TFNP from Sherali-Adams Lower Bounds
statement_tex:
\phantomsection
\label{def:uSAproofsyst}
    Let $F = \{D_i\}_{i \in [m]}$ be an unsatisfiable collection of DNFs (a collection with no shared satisfying assignment).
     A $\Sigma_2$-\emph{unary-Sherali-Adams} (denoted $\SA$) proof $\Pi$ of $F$ is a $\Sigma_2$-weakening $F' = \{D_i'\}_{i \in [m']}$ of $F$ 
    
    together with a list of conical juntas ${\cal J}_i, {\cal J}$, such that
    \[ \sum_{i \in [m']} D_i' {\cal J}_i + {\cal J} = -1. \]
     The \emph{degree} $\deg(\Pi)$ is the maximum degree among $D_i, D_i' {\cal J}_i,$ and ${\cal J}$, and the \emph{size} $\size(\Pi)$ is the number of monomials 
     in $D_i,D_i' {\cal J}_i, {\cal J}$
     counted with multiplicity (i.e., each monomial is counted again each time it appears). 
    The \emph{complexity} of the proof is given by $\SA(\Pi)~:=~ \deg(\Pi)+\log \size(\Pi)$, and the complexity of proving $F$ is $\SA(F)~:=~\min_{\Pi} \SA(\Pi)$, where the minimum is taken over all $\SA$ proofs $\Pi$ of $F$.
statement_text: phantomsection Let F = {D_i}_ i ∈ [m] be an unsatisfiable collection of DNFs (a collection with no shared satisfying assignment). A Σ_2 - unary-Sherali-Adams (denoted SA ) proof Π of F is a Σ_2 -weakening F' = {D_i'}_ i ∈ [m'] of F together with a list of conical juntas cal J _i, cal J , such that \[ Σ _ i ∈ [m'] D_i' cal J _i + cal J = -1. \] The degree deg (Π) is the maximum degree among D_i, D_i' cal J _i, and cal J , and the size size (Π) is the number of monomials in D_i,D_i' cal J _i, cal J counted with multiplicity (i.e., each monomial is counted again each time it appears). The complexity of the proof is given by SA (Π) := deg (Π)+ log size (Π) , and the complexity of proving F is SA (F) := min _ Π SA (Π) , where the minimum is taken over all SA proofs Π of F .

statement_text: AP Let n ∈ \?N . We define the AP ""zigzag graph"" intro *zigzag n 2 of width n and length 2 to be "graph@@dir" whose vertices are a_0, dotsc , a_n , b_0, dotsc , b_ n , a'_0 and b'_n , with edges from a_i to b_ i-1 and to b_ i (for i ∈ intInt 0,n , whenever the nodes exist), and with an edge from a'_0 to a_0 and from b_n to b'_n . See Cref fig:zigzag-graph-hom-T2 for an illustration. Note that zigzag n 2 does not admit a "homomorphism" to the " 2 -path"---indeed, such a homomorphism should send a'_0 , a_0 and b_0 onto 0 , 1 , and 2 , respectively, and so all a_i 's (resp. b_i 's) must be sent onto 1 (resp. 2 ), but then b'_n cannot be mapped anywhere. We claim that each zigzag n 2 ( n ∈ N ) is a "critical obstruction" of pathGraph 2 . We have already seen that zigzag n 2 is an "obstruction" of pathGraph 2 . But then notice that to obtain a "proper substructure" of zigzag n 2 , we must either: remove the edge from a'_0 to a_0 or the edge from b_n to b'_n , in which case it admits a "homomorphism" to pathGraph 2 , or remove any other edge, in which case the resulting "substructure" is not "connected", and both parts admit a "homomorphism" to pathGraph 2 . And hence, by Cref prop:finite-duality-iff-critical-obstructions , it follows that pathGraph 2 does not have "finite duality". On the other hand, each zigzag n 2 with n ∈ Np admits a "homomorphism" to the " 2 -transitive tournament", as witnessed by Cref fig:zigzag-graph-hom-T2 . However, observe that zigzag 0 2 = pathGraph 3 is an "obstruction" of transitiveTournament 2 . In fact, this "homomorphism" is far from being unique: each vertex a_1, a_2, dotsc , a_ n-1 can be sent on either 0 or 1 (the red and yellow vertices), and similarly, each vertex b_1, b_2, dotsc , b_ n-1 can be sent on either 1 or 2 (the yellow and blue vertices).

label: ex:Feder-Vardi-P2
paper_title: A Dichotomy Theorem for Automatic Structures
statement_text: Using Cref prop:charac-Feder-Vardi , we can prove for instance that if a "graph@@dir" \?G has "tree duality", then either it is a "DAG", or \?G contains a self-loop. Indeed, let v_0 → v_1 → ... → v_m be a "directed cycle" in \?G , with v_0 = v_m . Then in FederVardi \?G , there is an edge from {v_0,v_1,dotsc ,v_m} to itself. Since \?G has "tree duality", it follows by Cref prop:charac-Feder-Vardi that FederVardi \?G homto \?G and hence \?G also contains a self-loop. Note that, if \?G contains a self-loop, then actually it is "homomorphically equivalent" to the graph consisting of a single self-loop---that admits varnothing as a "dual" and hence has "tree duality". In other words, what we showed can be rephrased as: any non-trivial "graph@@dir" with "tree duality" is a "DAG". For instance, this implies that clique 2 does not have "tree duality". On the other hand, we saw in Cref ex:zigzag-defn that pathGraph 2 does not have "finite duality". However, it has "tree duality": indeed, see Cref fig:P2-Feder-Vardi and observe that FederVardi pathGraph 2 homto pathGraph 2 .

paper_title: The Complexity of Sparse Win-Lose Bimatrix Games
statement_tex:
In a general polymatrix game, there are $n$ players with $m_i$ actions for player $i \in [n]$.
Let $a_i \in [m_i]$ be the action of player $i$. The payoff of player $i$ from the sub-game associated with player $j \neq i$ is determined by the matrix $A^{ij}$, where player $i$ gets a payoff of $A^{ij}_{a_i a_j}$ from this subgame if $i$ plays $a_i$ and $j$ plays $a_j$. Given the actions of all agents $(a_1, \ldots, a_n)$, the utility of player $i$ is equal to $\sum_{j \neq i} A^{ij}_{a_i a_j}$.
We make the following additional assumptions to restrict the class of polymatrix games we use in our reductions:
\begin{itemize}
    \item Each player has exactly two actions: $a_i \in \{0, 1\}$ for all $i$.

    \item All the payoffs are from the set $\{0, 1, 2\}$: $A^{ij} \in \{0, 1, 2\}^{2 \times 2}$ for all $i$ and $j \neq i$.

    \item All payoff matrices are either diagonal or anti-diagonal: for every $i$ and $j \neq i$, either $A^{ij}_{01} = A^{ij}_{10} = 0$ or $A^{ij}_{00} = A^{ij}_{11} = 0$.

    

    \item The game is \textit{bipartite}: We can view the polymatrix game as a directed graph, where the vertices are the players, and there is an edge from player $j$ to player $i$ if $A^{ij} \neq 0$. We assume that the underlying undirected graph of this directed graph is bipartite.

    \item The \textit{in-degree} is at most two: The payoff of any player depends upon at most two other players, i.e., for every player $i$, there exist at most two players $k$ and $k'$ such that $A^{ij} = 0$ for all $j \notin \{ k, k' \}$.
    

    \item The \textit{out-degree} is at most two: Any player can affect the payoff of at most two other players, i.e., for every player $i$, there exist at most two players $k$ and $k'$ such that $A^{ji} = 0$ for all $j \notin \{ k, k' \}$.
    
    
    
    
    

    

\end{itemize}
The $\eps$-\POLY{} problem is to find an $\eps$-WSNE of a polymatrix game satisfying the assumptions given above, for a given $\eps > 0$.

The payoff of player i from the sub-game associated with player j ≠ i is determined by the matrix A^ ij , where player i gets a payoff of A^ ij _ a_i a_j from this subgame if i plays a_i and j plays a_j . All payoff matrices are either diagonal or anti-diagonal: for every i and j ≠ i , either A^ ij _ 01 = A^ ij _ 10 = 0 or A^ ij _ 00 = A^ ij _ 11 = 0 . The game is it bipartite : We can view the polymatrix game as a directed graph, where the vertices are the players, and there is an edge from player j to player i if A^ ij ≠ 0 . statement_tex:
\label{def:stage1}
A game $(A, B)$ is a stage 1 game if all of the following hold.
Every column of $A$ and $B^\intercal$ contains either
(i) At most three non-zero payoffs in the set $\{1, 2\}$ with at most one
$2$, or
(ii) A single $4$ payoff along with at most three $1$s.
Every row of $A$ and $B^\intercal$ contains either
(i) At most three $1$ payoffs, or
(ii) A single $2$ along with at most one $1$, or
(iii) Exactly two $4$ payoffs.

statement_tex:
\label{def:xor_gadget}
    Let $p$ be a nonnegative integer.
    The \defi{XOR~gadget} of order~$p$ is a graph containing two paths $(a_1, \dots, a_{p})$ and $(b_1, \dots, b_{p})$ which are called the \defi{rails} of the XOR~gadget.
    In addition, for $i \in \{1, \dots, p\}$, the XOR~gadget contains vertex disjoint paths of length two with $a_i$ and $b_i$ as endpoints.  A \defi{subtour} of the XOR~gadget is a spanning path with two endpoints in the set $\{a_1, a_p, b_1, b_p\}$.
    For convenience, when $p = 0$, both the XOR~gadget of order zero and its only subtour are defined to be the empty graph.
statement_text: Let p be a nonnegative integer. The color defblue XOR gadget of order p is a graph containing two paths (a_1, ... , a_ p ) and (b_1, ... , b_ p ) which are called the color defblue rails of the XOR gadget. In addition, for i ∈ {1, ... , p} , the XOR gadget contains vertex disjoint paths of length two with a_i and b_i as endpoints. A color defblue subtour of the XOR gadget is a spanning path with two endpoints in the set {a_1, a_p, b_1, b_p} . For convenience, when p = 0 , both the XOR gadget of order zero and its only subtour are defined to be the empty graph.

label: lem:end_doors
paper_title: On the PLS-Completeness of $k$-Opt Local Search for the Traveling Salesman Problem
statement_text: For any tour of G and any H -vertex x , the tour contains either both the door incident to x_ ell and the closest door to x_r or none of them. Further, these two doors are in the tour, if and only if the left and right first-set edges of x are not in the tour.
