statement_text: Consider a system of linear equations Ax=b in unknown x ∈ R ^d , where A ∈ {0,1}^ m × d and b ∈ {0,1}^d have zero-one entries. If the system has a solution, then it has a rational solution x^star ∈ Q ^d such that |x^star |_1 ≤ m^ m+1 .

label: eq:efron-stein
paper_title: Strongly Refuting Random CSP without Literals
statement_tex:
Let $\nu^k$ be a product distribution over $D^k$.
  Given a subset $S \subseteq [k]$, define $Y_S$ to be the vector space of $S$-juntas $Z_S$ to be the subspace of $Y_S$
  orthogonal to all the subspaces of proper subsets of $S$:
  \[ Z_S \coloneqq Y_S \cap \Span\set{Y_T | T \subsetneq S}^\perp \quad \text{under } \nu^S. \]
  The subspaces $\set{Z_S | S \subseteq [k]}$ are mutually orthogonal under $\nu^k$ and together they span
  $L^2(\nu^k)$.
  The Efron--Stein decomposition is the orthogonal decomposition
  \begin{equation} \label{eq:efron-stein}
    L^2 (\nu^k) = \bigoplus_{S \subseteq [k]} Z_S \quad \text{under } \nu^k.
  \end{equation}
statement_text: Let ν^k be a product distribution over D^k . Given a subset S ⊆ [k] , define Y_S to be the vector space of S -juntas Z_S to be the subspace of Y_S orthogonal to all the subspaces of proper subsets of S : \[ Z_S coloneqq Y_S ∩ span set Y_T | T ⊊ S ^perp quad under ν^S. \] The subspaces set Z_S | S ⊆ [k] are mutually orthogonal under ν^k and together they span L^2(ν^k) . The Efron--Stein decomposition is the orthogonal decomposition L^2 (ν^k) = oplus_ S ⊆ [k] Z_S quad under ν^k.
title: Efron--Stein

label: lem:independent-error
paper_title: Strongly Refuting Random CSP without Literals
statement_tex:
\label{lem:independent-error}
  For $t \in \N$, let $U_t$ be the uniform distribution over $[n]^{\underline t}$.
  Then $\norm{U_{s+t} - U_s U_t}_{\ell_1} = O(1/n)$ for any $s,t \in \N$.
  In particular, $\norm{U_{2s} - U_s U_s}_{\ell_1} = O(1/n)$ for any $s \in \N$.
statement_text: For t ∈ N , let U_t be the uniform distribution over [n]^ underline t . Then norm U_ s+t - U_s U_t _ ell _1 = O(1/n) for any s,t ∈ N . In particular, norm U_ 2s - U_s U_s _ ell _1 = O(1/n) for any s ∈ N .

label: lem:product-close
paper_title: Strongly Refuting Random CSP without Literals
statement_tex:
\label{lem:product-close}
  Suppose $\nu_i$ and $\eta_i$ are distributions over a common finite probability space $\Omega_i$, for $1
  \leq i \leq t$.
  Let $\nu \coloneqq \prod_{1 \leq i \leq t} \nu_i$ and $\eta \coloneqq \prod_{1 \leq i \leq t} \eta_i$ be their product
  distributions.
  Then
  \[ \Norm{\nu - \eta}_{\ell_1} \leq \sum_{1 \leq i \leq t} \Norm{\nu_i - \eta_i}_{\ell_1}. \]
statement_text: Suppose ν_i and η_i are distributions over a common finite probability space Ω_i , for 1 ≤ i ≤ t . Let ν coloneqq Π _ 1 ≤ i ≤ t ν_i and η coloneqq Π _ 1 ≤ i ≤ t η_i be their product distributions. Then \[ lVert ν - η rVert _ ell _1 ≤ Σ _ 1 ≤ i ≤ t lVert ν_i - η_i rVert _ ell _1 . \]

paper_title: Strongly Refuting Random CSP without Literals
statement_text: Given any distributions ν and η over a finite probability space Ω , and any distribution μ over a finite probability space Γ , \[ norm ν × μ - η × μ _ ell _1 = norm ν - η _ ell _1 . \]

label: random-unsat

statement_tex:
\label{random-unsat}
  Consider a distribution $\rho$ over $D^k$.
  As long as $\Delta \geq \exp(O(|D|^k))$, except with probability $o_{n;|D|,k}(1)$ over a binomial $\rho$-random
  $k$-CSP instance $\cI = (V, \cC)$ with $n$ variables and $\Delta n$ expected constraints,
  \[ \opt(\cI) = \opt_k(\rho) + o_{n;|D|,k}(1)\,. \]
statement_text: Consider a distribution ρ over D^k . As long as Δ ≥ exp (O(|D|^k)) , except with probability o_ n;|D|,k (1) over a binomial ρ -random k -CSP instance I = (V, C) with n variables and Δ n expected constraints, \[ opt (I) = opt _k(ρ) + o_ n;|D|,k (1) . \]

label: lem:random-expand
paper_title: Strongly Refuting Random CSP without Literals
statement_tex:
\label{lem:random-expand}
  Let $2 \leq \tau < k$, $\lambda \coloneqq \tau - 1$, $0 < \gamma \leq \lambda/2$,
  $\zeta \coloneqq \Delta^{2/(\lambda-\gamma)}/n$.
  Except with probability $o_{\zeta;k}(1)$, a random $k$-uniform undirected hypergraph with $n$ vertices
  and $\Delta n$ expected undirected hyperedges $\cH$ from the binomial model is $(t,\gamma)$-expanding, where
  \[ t = \frac n{\Delta^{2/(\lambda-\gamma)}} \cdot \frac 1{2^{O(k)}}. \]
statement_text: Let 2 ≤ τ < k , λ coloneqq τ - 1 , 0 < γ ≤ λ/2 , ζ coloneqq Δ^ 2/(λ-γ) /n . Except with probability o_ ζ;k (1) , a random k -uniform undirected hypergraph with n vertices and Δ n expected undirected hyperedges H from the binomial model is (t,γ) -expanding, where \[ t = frac n Δ^ 2/(λ-γ) · frac 1 2^ O(k) . \]

label: thm:poly-separator
paper_title: Strongly Refuting Random CSP without Literals
statement_tex:
\label{thm:poly-separator}
  Let $R \subseteq D^k$.
  There is a $t$-wise $\nu$-independent distribution $\eta$ such that $\supp(\eta) \subseteq R$ if and only if there is
  no degree-$t$ polynomial $f \in L^2(D^k, \nu^k)$ such that $f(a) > \E_{\nu^k} [f]$ for every $a \in R$.
statement_text: Let R ⊆ D^k . There is a t -wise ν -independent distribution η such that normal supp (η) ⊆ R if and only if there is no degree- t polynomial f ∈ L^2(D^k, ν^k) such that f(a) > mathop E _ ν^k [f] for every a ∈ R .

label: thm:indep-not-uniform
paper_title: Strongly Refuting Random CSP without Literals
statement_tex:
\label{thm:indep-not-uniform}
  Fix any $0 < p < 1/16$.
  Consider the $p$-biased distribution $\nu_p$ over $\set{0,1}$ where $\nu_p (1) = p$.
  Given $s \in \N$, let $R$ be a collection of $s$ random strings over $\set{0,1}^k$ sampled independently
  with replacement from $\nu_p^k$.
  Except with probability $o_k(1)$, there is a $\nu_p$-independent distribution supported on $R$ but not
  any pairwise uniform distribution (even when restricted to subdomains), provided $s = \Theta(k^2)$.
statement_text: Fix any 0 < p < 1/16 . Consider the p -biased distribution ν_p over set 0,1 where ν_p (1) = p . Given s ∈ N , let R be a collection of s random strings over set 0,1 ^k sampled independently with replacement from ν_p^k . Except with probability o_k(1) , there is a ν_p -independent distribution supported on R but not any pairwise uniform distribution (even when restricted to subdomains), provided s = Θ(k^2) .

label: lem:bernstein
paper_title: Strongly Refuting Random CSP without Literals
statement_tex:
\label{lem:bernstein}
  Let $X_1, … X_\ell$ be independent $0$-mean random variables such that $\abs{X_e} \leq B$ for $e \in [\ell]$.
  Then for any $a > 0$,
    \[ \Pr\Brac{\sum_{e \in [\ell]} X_e > a} \leq 
    \exp\Paren{\frac{-\frac12 a^2}{\sum_{e \in [\ell]} \E[X_e^2] + \frac 13 Ba}}. \]
statement_text: Let X_1, … X_ell be independent 0 -mean random variables such that abs X_e ≤ B for e ∈ [ell ] . Then for any a > 0 , \[ mathop bf Pr [ Σ _ e ∈ [ell ] X_e > a ] ≤ exp (frac -frac 12 a^2 Σ _ e ∈ [ell ] mathop E [X_e^2] + frac 13 Ba ). \]

label: thm:tensor-norm-bound
paper_title: Strongly Refuting Random CSP without Literals
statement_tex:
\label{thm:tensor-norm-bound}
  Let $(T^1, \cdots, T^\ell)$ be independent random tensors on $[n]^t$ such that for every $e \in [\ell]$,
  \[ \E[T^e] = 0, \quad \E\Brac{\norm{M(T^e)}^2_{\infty\to1}} \leq p, \quad \norm{M(T^e)}_{\infty\to1} \leq B. \]
  For $t \geq 1, p \ell \geq n^{\ceil{t/2}}$, except with probability $o_n (1)$,
  \[ \Norm{M\Paren{\sum_{e \in [\ell]} T^e}}_{\infty\to1} \lesssim B \sqrt{p \ell n^{\ceil{t/2}}}. \]
statement_text: Let (T^1, ... , T^ell ) be independent random tensors on [n]^t such that for every e ∈ [ell ] , \[ mathop E [T^e] = 0, quad mathop E [norm M(T^e) ^2_ ∞ → 1 ] ≤ p, quad norm M(T^e) _ ∞ → 1 ≤ B. \] For t ≥ 1, p ell ≥ n^ ceil t/2 , except with probability o_n (1) , \[ lVertM ( Σ _ e ∈ [ell ] T^e ) rVert _ ∞ → 1 lesssim B sqrt p ell n^ ceil t/2 . \]

label: thm:avg-tensor-norm-bound

statement_tex:
\label{thm:avg-tensor-norm-bound}
  Fix $t \leq k$.

  For any $\eps > 0$, there is $C = C(T,\eps)$ such that for $p \geq C n^{\ceil{t/2} - k}$, except with probability
  $o_n (1)$, a random $k$-CSP instance $I = (V, \mathcal{C})$ on $n$ variables with constraint probability $p$ satisfies
  \[ \Norm{M(T^\cC - \overline T)}_{\infty\to1} \leq \eps. \]
statement_text: Fix t ≤ k . Let T be a tensor on ([k] × D)^ underline t . For any ε > 0 , there is C = C(T,ε) such that for p ≥ C n^ ceil t/2 - k , except with probability o_n (1) , a random k -CSP instance I = (V, C ) on n variables with constraint probability p satisfies \[ lVertM (T^C - overline T) rVert _ ∞ → 1 ≤ ε. \]

label: def:concentration-instance
paper_title: Strongly Refuting Random CSP without Literals
statement_tex:
\label{def:concentration-instance}
  Given $f^\Omega: \Omega_k \to \R, \eps > 0, d \in \N$, a constraint set $\cC$ over variable set $V$ is
  $(f^\Omega,\eps,d)$-concentrated if there is a degree-$d$ SOS proof of
  \[
    \Set{ \textstyle \sum_{a\in D} x_{v,a}^2 \leq 1}_{v \in V} \quad \vdash_d \quad \E_{\sigma \in \mathcal C}
    f^{\Omega,\sigma} (x) \leq \E_{\sigma \in V^{\underline k}} f^{\Omega,\sigma} (x) + \eps.
  \]
statement_text: Given f^Ω: Ω_k → R , ε > 0, d ∈ N , a constraint set C over variable set V is (f^Ω,ε,d) -concentrated if there is a degree- d SOS proof of \[ Set style Σ _ a ∈ D x_ v,a ^2 ≤ 1 _ v ∈ V quad vdash _d quad mathop E _ σ ∈ C f^ Ω,σ (x) ≤ mathop E _ σ ∈ V^ underline k f^ Ω,σ (x) + ε. \]

label: thm: mld_main
paper_title: Tight Lower Bound for Approximating Parametrized Maximum Likelihood Decoding under ETH
statement_text: Assuming ETH , there exist constants γ > 1 and δ>0 , such that for any algorithm that takes as input a matrix H ∈ F _q^ d × N , a vector u ∈ F _q^ d and a parameter k ∈ N , it must take N^ δ k time to distinguish the following two cases: sf YES Case: There exists x ∈ F _q^ N with | x |_0 ≤ k such that H x = u . sf NO Case: For every x ∈ F _q^ N with | x |_0 ≤ γ k , we have H x ≠ u .

label: def:colored-MLD
paper_title: Tight Lower Bound for Approximating Parametrized Maximum Likelihood Decoding under ETH
statement_tex:
\label{def:colored-MLD}
    The instance consists of $k$ vector multisets $V_1,\dots,V_k \subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^d$ each of size $n$, 
    and a target vector $\vec{t} \in \mathbb{F}_q^d$, with parameter $k$. The goal is to distinguish between the following cases.
    \begin{itemize}
    \item\yes Case: There exist $\vec{v}_i \in V_i$ for every $i \in [k]$ such that
    \[
    \vec{v}_1 + \cdots + \vec{v}_k = \vec{t}.
    \]
    
    \item\no Case: For any $\ell \le \gamma k$, any choice of 
    $\vec{v}_1,\dots,\vec{v}_\ell \in V_1 \cup \cdots \cup V_k$ and 
    $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_\ell \in \mathbb{F}_q$ satisfies
    \[
    \alpha_1 \vec{v}_1 + \cdots + \alpha_\ell \vec{v}_\ell \neq \vec{t}.

statement_tex:
A $(k,d)$-hypercube partition system is a pair $(U,\Fcal)$ where $U:=[k]^{[d]}$ and $\Fcal:=\{f_1,\dots,f_d\}$ is a collection of funtions from $U$ to $[k]$. We view $U$ as the set of all points in a $d$-dimensional hypercube where each coordinate takes a value in $[k]$. The $i$-th partition $f_i:U\to[k]$ is defined as for every $x\in U$
    $$
        f_i(x)=x(i).
    $$
    In other words, for any $x\in U$, $f_i$ groups $x$ according to its $i$-th coordinate, into the $x(i)$-th set.

statement_tex: A \emph{catalytic} Turing machine is a machine $M$ with four tapes: 1) a read-only input tape; 2) a write-only output tape; 3) a read-write work tape; and 4) a read-write \emph{catalytic} tape. $M$ has the property that for any initializations $x$ to the input tape and $\tau$ to the catalytic tape, $M$ halts with $\tau$ in the catalytic tape.

M has the property that for any initializations x to the input tape and τ to the catalytic tape, M halts with τ in the catalytic tape.

statement_tex: We define $\CSPACE{s}{c}$ to be the class of languages $L$ that can be decided by a catalytic machine with $s$ bits of work space and $c$ bits of catalytic space on inputs of length $n$, i.e., on input $x \in \{0,1\}^n$ and initial catalytic tape $\tau \in \{0,1\}^c$, $M$ halts with $L(x)$ in the output tape and $\tau$ in the catalytic tape.

paper_title: Understanding Robust Catalytic Computing
statement_tex:
A \emph{lossy catalytic Turing machine} with $e$ errors is a Turing machine $M$ with the same four tapes as a catalytic Turing machine, but where on any input $x$ and initial catalytic tape $\tau$, the machine must halt with some $\tau'$ in the catalytic tape such that $\tau$ and $\tau'$ differ in at most $e$ locations.

label: definition_config_graphs
paper_title: Understanding Robust Catalytic Computing
statement_tex:
\label{definition_config_graphs}
    The configuration graph \( \gmx \) is a directed acyclic graph where each node corresponds to a configuration of the machine \( M \) on input \( x \). There is a directed edge from \( \conf{\pi}{u} \) to \( \conf{\pi'}{u'} \) if and only if \( \conf{\pi'}{u'} \) can be reached from \( \conf{\pi}{u} \) in one execution step of \( M \). If \( M \) is a probabilistic machine, the out-degree of every vertex in \( \gmx \) is at most 2; if \( M \) is deterministic, the out-degree is at most 1. A halting configuration has no outgoing edges in \( \gmx \). Furthermore, there exists a fixed constant $d_M$, which depends solely on $M$, such that each vertex in $\gmx$ has at most $d_M$ incident edges.
statement_text: The configuration graph \( G_ M,x \) is a directed acyclic graph where each node corresponds to a configuration of the machine \( M \) on input \( x \). There is a directed edge from \( le π,u rangle \) to \( le π',u' rangle \) if and only if \( le π',u' rangle \) can be reached from \( le π,u rangle \) in one execution step of \( M \). If \( M \) is a probabilistic machine, the out-degree of every vertex in \( G_ M,x \) is at most 2; if \( M \) is deterministic, the out-degree is at most 1. A halting configuration has no outgoing edges in \( G_ M,x \). Furthermore, there exists a fixed constant d_M , which depends solely on M , such that each vertex in G_ M,x has at most d_M incident edges.

statement_text: Let \( M \) be a deterministic catalytic machine that utilizes \( s \) bits of work space and \( c \) bits of catalytic space. We have the following catalytic subroutines, which use extra \( O(s) \) bits of work space bf sc Next . Given le π,u rangle on catalytic tape and work tape, this subroutine replaces le π,u rangle with le π',u' rangle , which is the next vertex in (cyclic) pre-order traversal of G_ M,x (le π,u rangle ) . bf sc StepBack . Given le π,u rangle on catalytic tape and work tape, this subroutine replaces le π,u rangle with le π',u' rangle , which is the previous vertex in pre-order traversal of G_ M,x (le π,u rangle ) . bf sc Size . Given le π,u rangle on catalytic tape and work tape, and an integer S ≤ 2^ O(s) , this subroutine checks whether G_ M,x (le π,u rangle ) is of size at most S . It returns the content of le π,u rangle unchanged. The procedure bf sc Size runs in time 2^ O(s) , and the procedures bf sc Next and bf sc StepBack run in time 2^ O(s) · D where D is the depth of G_ M,x (le π,u rangle ) .

statement_tex:
\label{lem:ecc}
    There exists a compression scheme $(\text{Enc}_{\text{BCH}}, \text{Dec}_{\text{BCH}})$ such that:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item \textbf{Encoding:} \(\text{Enc}_{\text{BCH}}\) takes as input a string \( S \) of length \( c \), plus an additional \((2e + 1) \lceil \log(c + e) \rceil\) bits initialized to zero, and outputs a codeword \( S_{\text{enc}} \):
        \[
        S + [0]^{(2e+1)\lceil \log(c+e) \rceil} 
        \xrightarrow{\text{Enc}_{\text{BCH}}} 
        S_{\text{enc}}.
        \]
        Furthermore, all outputs \( S_{\text{enc}} \) generated this way have minimum distance \(\delta := 2e + 1\) from one another.
        
        \item \textbf{Decoding:} \(\text{Dec}_{\text{BCH}}\) takes as input a string \( S'_{\text{enc}} \) of length 
        \[
        c + (2e+1) \lceil \log(c+e) \rceil,
        \]
        with the promise that there exists a string \( S \) of length \( c \) such that 
        \[
        \text{Enc}_{\text{BCH}}\bigl(S + [0]^{(2e+1)\lceil \log(c+e)\rceil}\bigr)
        \]
        differs from \( S'_{\text{enc}} \) in at most \(\delta/2 - 1 = e\) locations, and outputs this string \( S \):
        \[
        S'_{\text{enc}} \xrightarrow{\text{Dec}_{\text{BCH}}} S + [0]^{(2e+1)\lceil \log(c+e)\rceil}.
        \]
        Furthermore, both \(\text{Enc}_{\text{BCH}}\) and \(\text{Dec}_{\text{BCH}}\) can be computed in space \( O(e \log c) \).
    \end{itemize}

\label{thm:cherExp}
Let $G = (V,E)$ be an $(n,d,\lambda)$-graph and let $f : V \to [0,1]$ be any function.

paper_title: Optimal Inapproximability of Generalized Linear Equations over a Finite Group
statement_tex: Consider a multiset of linear equations $(C_1,C_2,\dots, C_m)$ over variables $\{x_1,x_2,\dots,x_n|x_i\in G\}$ for a group $G$. Each constraint consists of a tuple of exactly $k$ literals and will be considered satisfied when their sum/product over $G$ is in $S\subseteq G$. The $\text{Max-E$k$-LIN}_{S}(G)$ problem is to find an assignment to $\{x_1,x_2,\dots,x_n\}$ that maximizes the number of satisfied constraints.

Each constraint consists of a tuple of exactly k literals and will be considered satisfied when their sum/product over G is in S ⊆ G . The Max-E k -LIN _ S (G) problem is to find an assignment to {x_1,x_2, ... ,x_n} that maximizes the number of satisfied constraints.

label: thm:main

statement_text: Fix any finite group G and S ⊆ G . Furthermore, if S^ -1 S generates H_S , assuming P ≠ NP , for every ε>0 , it is NP -hard to approximate Max-E k -LIN _ S (G) within a factor of frac |S| |H_S| +ε .

label: def:label-cover
paper_title: Optimal Inapproximability of Generalized Linear Equations over a Finite Group
statement_tex:
\label{def:label-cover} An instance $\Psi=(U,V,E,[L],
		[R],\{\pi_e\}_{e\in E})$ of the {\LC} constraint satisfaction
		problem consists of a bi-regular bipartite graph $(U,V,E)$,
		   alphabets $[L]$ and $[R]$ and a surjective projection map $\pi_e : [L] \rightarrow
		[R]$ for every edge $e\in E$. 
		Given a labeling $\ell : U \rightarrow [L], \ell:V \rightarrow
		[R]$, an edge $e = (u,v)$ is said to be satisfied by $\ell$ if
		$\pi_e(\ell(u)) = \ell(v)$. 
		
		$\Psi$ is said to be \emph{satisfiable} if there exists a 
		labeling that satisfies all the
		edges. $\Psi$ is said to be \emph{at most $\delta$-satisfiable} if every
		labeling satisfies at most a $\delta$ fraction of the
		edges.
statement_text: An instance Ψ=(U,V,E,[L], [R],{π_e}_ e ∈ E ) of the Label Cover constraint satisfaction problem consists of a bi-regular bipartite graph (U,V,E) , alphabets [L] and [R] and a surjective projection map π_e : [L] → [R] for every edge e ∈ E . Given a labeling ell : U → [L], ell :V → [R] , an edge e = (u,v) is said to be satisfied by ell if π_e(ell (u)) = ell (v) . Ψ is said to be satisfiable if there exists a labeling that satisfies all the edges. Ψ is said to be at most δ -satisfiable if every labeling satisfies at most a δ fraction of the edges.
title: Label Cover

label: thm:LChard
paper_title: Optimal Inapproximability of Generalized Linear Equations over a Finite Group
statement_tex:
\label{thm:LChard} For every $r \in \N$, there is a deterministic $n^{O(r)}$-time reduction from a \TSAT\ instance
		of size $n$ to an instance $\Psi=(U,V,E,[L],[R], \{\pi_e\}_{e\in E})$ of \LC\ with the following properties: $|U|,|V| \leq n^{O(r)}$; $L,R \leq 2^{O(r)}$; $\Psi$ is bi-regular with degrees bounded by $2^{O(r)}$.
			
			\begin{itemize}
				
				\item YES Case : If the \TSAT\ instance is
				satisfiable, then $\Psi$ is satisfiable.
				
				\item NO Case : If the \TSAT\ instance is
				unsatisfiable, then $\Psi$ is
				at most $2^{-r}$-satisfiable.
			\end{itemize}
statement_text: For every r ∈ N , there is a deterministic n^ O(r) -time reduction from a 3 - SAT\ instance of size n to an instance Ψ=(U,V,E,[L],[R], {π_e}_ e ∈ E ) of Label Cover \ with the following properties: |U|,|V| leqslant n^ O(r) ; L,R leqslant 2^ O(r) ; Ψ is bi-regular with degrees bounded by 2^ O(r) . YES Case : If the 3 - SAT\ instance is satisfiable, then Ψ is satisfiable. NO Case : If the 3 - SAT\ instance is unsatisfiable, then Ψ is at most 2^ -r -satisfiable.
title: Hardness of Label Cover

paper_title: Optimal Inapproximability of Generalized Linear Equations over a Finite Group
statement_tex: An $T$-\LLC\ instance, given by $\mathcal{H}=(\mathcal{V}=\{V_1,\dots,V_T\}, \{\Pi_{i,j}\}_{1\leq i < j\leq T}\}, \{[R_i]_{i\in [T]}\}$ consist of $T$ sets of vertices $\mathcal{V}=\{V_1,\dots,V_T\}$. The label set of vertices in layer $i$ is denoted by $[R_i]$. Every pair of layers $1\le i<j\le l$ has a set of constraints $\Pi_{i,j}$ between the vertices in $V_{i}$ and $V_{j}$. The constraint between $v\in V_{i}$ and $u\in V_{j}$ (if it exists in $\Pi_{i,j}$) is denoted by $\pi_{vu}$. Moreover, every constraint between a pair of vertices is a projection constraint: for every assignment $k\in[R_{i}]$ to $v\in V_{i}$, there is a unique assignment to $u\in V_{j}$ that satisfies the constraint $\pi_{vu}$.
statement_text: An T - Layered Label Cover \ instance, given by H =( V ={V_1, ... ,V_T}, {Π_ i,j }_ 1leqslant i < jleqslant T }, {[R_i]_ i ∈ [T] } consist of T sets of vertices V ={V_1, ... ,V_T} . The label set of vertices in layer i is denoted by [R_i] . Every pair of layers 1 ≤ i<j ≤ l has a set of constraints Π_ i,j between the vertices in V_ i and V_ j . The constraint between v ∈ V_ i and u ∈ V_ j (if it exists in Π_ i,j ) is denoted by π_ vu . Moreover, every constraint between a pair of vertices is a projection constraint: for every assignment k ∈ [R_ i ] to v ∈ V_ i , there is a unique assignment to u ∈ V_ j that satisfies the constraint π_ vu .
title: Layered Label Cover

label: thm:layered_lc_hardness
paper_title: Optimal Inapproximability of Generalized Linear Equations over a Finite Group
statement_text: For any constant parameters T ≥ 2 , r ∈ Z , the following problem is NP-hard. Given an T - Layered Label Cover \ instance H =( V ={V_ 1 ,...,V_ T },{Π_ i,j }_ 1 ≤ i<j ≤ T ,{[R_ t ]}_ t ∈ [T] ) where all variable ranges R_ t are of size 2^ O(Tr) , distinguish between the following two cases: bf Completeness. There is an assignment satisfying all the constraints of the Label Cover instance. In this case, we say that H is fully satisfiable. bf Soundness. For every 1 ≤ i<j ≤ T , no assignment satisfies more than a 2^ -r fraction of the set of constraints Π_ i,j between layers i and j . In this case, we say that H is at most 2^ -r -satisfiable.

statement_tex:
Let $X = \sum_{i=1}^m X_i$, where $X_i$ are independent Bernoulli random variables, and let $\mu = \mathbb{E}[X]$. Then for any $0 < \delta < 1$,
\[
\Pr\!\left[X \leq (1-\delta)\mu \right] \;\leq\; \exp\!\left(-\frac{\delta^2}{2}\mu\right),
\]
and for any $\delta > 0$,
\[
\Pr\!\left[X \geq (1+\delta)\mu \right] \;\leq\; \exp\!\left(-\frac{\delta^2}{2+\delta}\mu\right).
\]

\]

Let $\bm X_1,\dots,\bm X_n$ be independent $\{0,1\}$-valued random variables, and let
$\bm X = \sum_{i=1}^n \bm X_i$, $ 
\mu = \mathbb{E}[\bm X].

Then, for $0\leq \delta\leq 1$,
\begin{align*}
\Pr\left[\bm X \geq (1+\delta)\mu\right] \leq \exp\left(-\frac{\mu \delta^2}{3}\right),
\\

\end{align*}

statement_text: Let S ⊇ S^1_2 be finitely axiomatized and sequential, and let φ be true. If EA vdash Con _ S → Con _ S + φ , then there is a polynomial p such that S sststile n^ O(1) Con _ S (p(n)) → Con _ S + φ (n) . In particular, S sststile n^ O(1) Con _ S + φ (n) .

label: conj:HRC
paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
statement_tex:
\label{conj:HRC}
Let $\mathcal S{\supseteq}\Sone$ be a sound, finitely axiomatized sequential theory, and let $\phi$ be a true sentence. If $\EA{\not\vdash}\Con_{\mathcal S}{\rightarrow}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}\phi}$, then for every constant $c{>}0$, $\mathcal S\centernot{\sststile{}{n^c}}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}\phi}(n)$.\footnote{We expect the non-simulation implications of \textbf{HRC}/\textbf{FR}, \textbf{KH}, and related conjectures to extend to sound effective theories beyond the finitely axiomatized sequential class; no corresponding biconditional characterization is claimed there.}
statement_text: Let S ⊇ S^1_2 be a sound, finitely axiomatized sequential theory, and let φ be a true sentence. If EA not vdash Con _ S → Con _ S + φ , then for every constant c > 0 , Scenternot sststile n^c Con _ S + φ (n) . We expect the non-simulation implications of bf HRC /bf FR , bf KH , and related conjectures to extend to sound effective theories beyond the finitely axiomatized sequential class; no corresponding biconditional characterization is claimed there.
title: Higher Relative Consistency, bf HRC

label: conj:feasible-reflection
paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
statement_tex:
\label{conj:feasible-reflection}
(\textbf{Feasible Reflection (FR)}) Let $\mathcal S{\supseteq}\Sone$ be a sound, finitely axiomatized, sequential theory, and let $\phi$ be a true sentence. If $\mathcal S{\sststile{}{n^{O(1)}}}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}\phi}(n)$, then $\EA{\vdash}\Con_{\mathcal S}{\rightarrow}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}\phi}$.
statement_text: (bf Feasible Reflection (FR) ) Let S ⊇ S^1_2 be a sound, finitely axiomatized, sequential theory, and let φ be a true sentence. If S sststile n^ O(1) Con _ S + φ (n) , then EA vdash Con _ S → Con _ S + φ .

label: prop:hrc-fr-equivalence
paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
statement_tex:
\label{prop:hrc-fr-equivalence}
\textbf{HRC} (Conjecture~\ref{conj:HRC}) is equivalent to \textbf{FR} (Conjecture~\ref{conj:feasible-reflection}).
statement_text: bf HRC (Conjecture ) is equivalent to bf FR (Conjecture ).

label: thm:busy-beaver-transfer
paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
statement_text: For a sound theory S ⊇ S^1_2 , the following are equivalent. There exists a true sentence φ such that, for every constant c > 0 , Scenternot sststile n^c Con _ S + φ (n) . For all sufficiently large k and every constant c > 0 , Scenternot sststile n^c Con _ S^1_2 + φ_ BB (k) (n) .

label: conj:kolmogorov-hardness
paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
statement_tex:
\label{conj:kolmogorov-hardness}
(\textbf{Kolmogorov Hardness (KH)}) Let $\mathcal S{\supseteq}\Sone$ be a sound, finitely axiomatized, sequential theory. For every $x{\in}R$ in the standard model, one has $\mathcal S{\sststile{}{n^{O(1)}}}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}(x{\in}R)}(n)$ if and only if $\EA{\vdash}\Con_{\mathcal S}{\rightarrow}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}(x{\in}R)}$.\footnote{We expect the hardness direction of \textbf{KH} to extend to sound computably axiomatized ambient theories, whose sufficiently long true randomness facts remain inaccessible by Chaitin incompleteness.}
statement_text: (bf Kolmogorov Hardness (KH) ) Let S ⊇ S^1_2 be a sound, finitely axiomatized, sequential theory. For every x ∈ R in the standard model, one has S sststile n^ O(1) Con _ S + (x ∈ R) (n) if and only if EA vdash Con _ S → Con _ S + (x ∈ R) . We expect the hardness direction of bf KH to extend to sound computably axiomatized ambient theories, whose sufficiently long true randomness facts remain inaccessible by Chaitin incompleteness.

label: theoremHRCImpliesKH
paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
statement_tex:
\label{theoremHRCImpliesKH}
\textbf{HRC} implies \textbf{KH}. Moreover, assume \textbf{HRC}, let $\mathcal S{\supseteq}\Sone$ be a sound, finitely axiomatized, sequential theory, and let $x{\in}R$ hold in the standard model. If $\EA{+}\Con_{\mathcal S}{\not\vdash}x{\in}R$, then $\mathcal S\centernot{\sststile{}{n^{O(1)}}}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}(x{\in}R)}(n)$.
statement_text: bf HRC implies bf KH . Moreover, assume bf HRC , let S ⊇ S^1_2 be a sound, finitely axiomatized, sequential theory, and let x ∈ R hold in the standard model. If EA + Con _ S not vdash x ∈ R , then Scenternot sststile n^ O(1) Con _ S + (x ∈ R) (n) .

label: lem:no-access-no-relative-consistency
paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
statement_tex:
\label{lem:no-access-no-relative-consistency}
For each fixed string $x$, if $\EA{+}\Con_{\mathcal S}{\not\vdash}x{\in}R$, then $\EA{\not\vdash}\Con_{\mathcal S}{\rightarrow}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}(x{\in}R)}$.
statement_text: For each fixed string x , if EA + Con _ S not vdash x ∈ R , then EA not vdash Con _ S → Con _ S + (x ∈ R) .

label: thm:robustness
paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
statement_tex:
\label{thm:robustness}
Let $U,U'$ be universal machines with Kolmogorov invariance constant $c=c(U,U')$, so that $|K_U(x)-K_{U'}(x)|\le c$ for every $x$. Fix $d\ge3$ and write $R_U^{(d)}:=\{x:K_U(x)\ge |x|-d\log|x|\}$. Then, for all sufficiently long $x$,
\[
x\in R_U^{(d)}\Longrightarrow x\in R_{U'}^{(d+1)}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
x\in R_{U'}^{(d)}\Longrightarrow x\in R_U^{(d+1)}.
\]
Consequently, the density estimates and conclusions depending only on those estimates are robust under changing the universal machine, after increasing the logarithmic-deficiency parameter and disregarding finitely many lengths.
statement_text: Let U,U' be universal machines with Kolmogorov invariance constant c=c(U,U') , so that |K_U(x)-K_ U' (x)| ≤ c for every x . Fix d ≥ 3 and write R_U^ (d) :={x:K_U(x) ≥ |x|-d log |x|} . Then, for all sufficiently long x , \[ x ∈ R_U^ (d) Longrightarrow x ∈ R_ U' ^ (d+1) qquad and qquad x ∈ R_ U' ^ (d) Longrightarrow x ∈ R_U^ (d+1) . \] Consequently, the density estimates and conclusions depending only on those estimates are robust under changing the universal machine, after increasing the logarithmic-deficiency parameter and disregarding finitely many lengths.

label: def:simulation-game
paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
statement_tex:
\label{def:simulation-game}
Let $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{fs}}$ be the class of sound, finitely axiomatized sequential theories extending $\Sone$, and let $\Phi$ be a family of true sentences. In the game $G(\Phi)$, Nature selects $\mathcal S{\in}\mathcal C_{\mathrm{fs}}$; the Theorist, seeing $\mathcal S$, selects $\phi{\in}\Phi$. Nature wins the round if $\mathcal S{\sststile{}{n^{O(1)}}}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}\phi}(n)$, and the Theorist wins if, for every constant $c$, $\mathcal S\centernot{\sststile{}{n^c}}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}\phi}(n)$. Exactly one player wins each round.\footnote{The outcomes are complementary: the negation of ``there is a constant $c$ with proofs of size at most $n^c$ for all sufficiently large $n$'' is ``for every $c$ there are infinitely many $n$ without proofs of size $n^c$,'' which is the hardness form used throughout.}
statement_text: Let C_ fs be the class of sound, finitely axiomatized sequential theories extending S^1_2 , and let Φ be a family of true sentences. In the game G(Φ) , Nature selects S ∈ C_ fs ; the Theorist, seeing S , selects φ ∈ Φ . Nature wins the round if S sststile n^ O(1) Con _ S + φ (n) , and the Theorist wins if, for every constant c , Scenternot sststile n^c Con _ S + φ (n) . Exactly one player wins each round.
title: Simulation game

label: def:explanation
paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
statement_tex:
\label{def:explanation}
A position $(\mathcal S,\phi)$ is \emph{explained} if $\EA{\vdash}\Con_{\mathcal S}{\rightarrow}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}\phi}$; the $\EA$-proof is the explanation, a certificate any third party can check without reference to the internals of~$\mathcal S$. Nature \emph{holds hidden information} at $(\mathcal S,\phi)$ if Nature wins at an unexplained position.
statement_text: A position (S,φ) is explained if EA vdash Con _ S → Con _ S + φ ; the EA -proof is the explanation, a certificate any third party can check without reference to the internals of S . Nature holds hidden information at (S,φ) if Nature wins at an unexplained position.
title: Explanation and hidden information

label: prop:explained-wins
paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
statement_tex:
\label{prop:explained-wins}
If $\mathcal S$ is finitely axiomatized and sequential and the position $(\mathcal S,\phi)$ is explained, then Nature wins at $(\mathcal S,\phi)$, by the canonical strategy: the explanation yields an interpretation of $\mathcal S{+}\phi$ in $\mathcal S$, whose proof translation supplies the required bounded-consistency proofs.
statement_text: If S is finitely axiomatized and sequential and the position (S,φ) is explained, then Nature wins at (S,φ) , by the canonical strategy: the explanation yields an interpretation of S + φ in S , whose proof translation supplies the required bounded-consistency proofs.
title: Explained positions are Nature wins

label: prop:random-strategy
paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
statement_tex:
\label{prop:random-strategy}
Assume \textbf{HRC}, and let the Theorist play true random axioms, $\Phi{=}\{x{\in}R:x{\in}R\ \text{is true}\}$. Then against every Nature move $\mathcal S$, at most finitely many rounds are Nature wins.
statement_text: Assume bf HRC , and let the Theorist play true random axioms, Φ = {x ∈ R:x ∈ R\ is true } . Then against every Nature move S , at most finitely many rounds are Nature wins.
title: The random-string strategy

label: lem:finite-certified-randomness
paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
statement_tex:
\label{lem:finite-certified-randomness}
The set $C_{\mathrm{rel}}^{\mathcal S}$ is finite. Hence there is an integer $k_R^{\mathcal S}$ such that, whenever $|x|{>}k_R^{\mathcal S}$ and $x{\in}R$ is true, one has $\EA{\not\vdash}\Con_{\mathcal S}{\rightarrow}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}(x{\in}R)}$.
statement_text: The set C_ rel ^ S is finite. Hence there is an integer k_R^ S such that, whenever |x| > k_R^ S and x ∈ R is true, one has EA not vdash Con _ S → Con _ S + (x ∈ R) .

label: conj:SETHKfinite
paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
statement_tex:
\label{conj:SETHKfinite}
Assume $\mathcal S$ is finitely axiomatized and sequential, and assume $\mathcal S\sststile{}{n^{O(1)}}\Con_{\mathcal S}(n)$. For every $m{>}k_R^{\mathcal S}$ and every $\epsilon$ with $0{<}\epsilon{<}1$, there exists $N_{R,m,\epsilon}^{\mathcal S}$ such that, for every true $x{\in}R\cap\{0,1\}^m$ and every $n{>}N_{R,m,\epsilon}^{\mathcal S}$, one has $\mathcal S\vdash_{\leq 2^{(1-\epsilon)n}}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}(x{\in}R)}(n)$ if and only if $\EA{\vdash}\Con_{\mathcal S}{\rightarrow}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}(x{\in}R)}$.
statement_text: Assume S is finitely axiomatized and sequential, and assume Ssststile n^ O(1) Con _ S (n) . For every m > k_R^ S and every ε with 0 < ε < 1 , there exists N_ R,m,ε ^ S such that, for every true x ∈ R ∩ {0,1}^m and every n > N_ R,m,ε ^ S , one has Svdash _ ≤ 2^ (1-ε)n Con _ S + (x ∈ R) (n) if and only if EA vdash Con _ S → Con _ S + (x ∈ R) .
title: bf SETH-K-Finite

label: theoremdensity
paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
statement_tex:
\label{theoremdensity}
Assume \textbf{SETH-K-Finite}. For every $m{>}k_R^{\mathcal S}$ and every $\epsilon$ with $0{<}\epsilon{<}1$, there exists $N_{R,m,\epsilon}^{\mathcal S}$ such that, for every $n{>}N_{R,m,\epsilon}^{\mathcal S}$, at least $(1{-}O(m^{-d}))2^m$ strings $x{\in}\{0,1\}^m$ satisfy $x{\in}R$ and $\mathcal S\nvdash_{\leq 2^{(1-\epsilon)n}}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}(x{\in}R)}(n)$.
statement_text: Assume bf SETH-K-Finite . For every m > k_R^ S and every ε with 0 < ε < 1 , there exists N_ R,m,ε ^ S such that, for every n > N_ R,m,ε ^ S , at least (1 - O(m^ -d ))2^m strings x ∈ {0,1}^m satisfy x ∈ R and Snvdash _ ≤ 2^ (1-ε)n Con _ S + (x ∈ R) (n) .

label: cor:no-intermediate-density
paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
statement_tex:
\label{cor:no-intermediate-density}
Assume \textbf{SETH-K-Finite}. For every $m{>}k_R^{\mathcal S}$ and every $\epsilon$ with $0{<}\epsilon{<}1$, there exists $N_{R,m,\epsilon}^{\mathcal S}$ such that, for every $n{>}N_{R,m,\epsilon}^{\mathcal S}$, one has $|H_{m,n,\epsilon}^{\mathcal S}|{\geq}(1{-}O(m^{-d}))2^m$.
statement_text: Assume bf SETH-K-Finite . For every m > k_R^ S and every ε with 0 < ε < 1 , there exists N_ R,m,ε ^ S such that, for every n > N_ R,m,ε ^ S , one has |H_ m,n,ε ^ S | ≥ (1 - O(m^ -d ))2^m .

label: cor:dense-small-hard-tautologies
paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
statement_tex:
\label{cor:dense-small-hard-tautologies}
Assume \textbf{SETH-K-Finite}, and assume that for some constant $a$ the chosen feasible correspondence between the bounded-consistency formalization and its propositional translation carries every propositional proof of $\tau_{x,n}$ of size $s$ to an $\mathcal S$-proof of $\Con_{\mathcal S{+}(x{\in}R)}(n)$ of size at most $s{\cdot}(m{+}n)^a$. For every $m{>}k_R^{\mathcal S}$ and every $\epsilon$ with $0{<}\epsilon{<}1$, there exists $\widetilde N_{R,m,\epsilon}^{\mathcal S}$ such that, for every $n{>}\widetilde N_{R,m,\epsilon}^{\mathcal S}$, at least $(1{-}O(m^{-d}))2^m$ strings $x{\in}\{0,1\}^m$ index tautologies $\tau_{x,n}$ of size $(m{+}n)^{O(1)}$ that require size greater than $2^{(1-\epsilon)n}$ in the propositional proof system associated with $\mathcal S$.
statement_text: Assume bf SETH-K-Finite , and assume that for some constant a the chosen feasible correspondence between the bounded-consistency formalization and its propositional translation carries every propositional proof of τ_ x,n of size s to an S -proof of Con _ S + (x ∈ R) (n) of size at most s · (m + n)^a . For every m > k_R^ S and every ε with 0 < ε < 1 , there exists widetilde N_ R,m,ε ^ S such that, for every n > widetilde N_ R,m,ε ^ S , at least (1 - O(m^ -d ))2^m strings x ∈ {0,1}^m index tautologies τ_ x,n of size (m + n)^ O(1) that require size greater than 2^ (1-ε)n in the propositional proof system associated with S .

label: theoremPairwiseRelativeConsistencyImpliesAccess
paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
statement_tex:
\label{theoremPairwiseRelativeConsistencyImpliesAccess}
For every pair of strings $x,y$, if $\EA{\vdash}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}(y{\in}R)}{\rightarrow}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}(x{\in}R)}$, then $\EA{+}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}(y{\in}R)}{\vdash}x{\in}R$.
statement_text: For every pair of strings x,y , if EA vdash Con _ S + (y ∈ R) → Con _ S + (x ∈ R) , then EA + Con _ S + (y ∈ R) vdash x ∈ R .

label: corollaryPairwiseFactualNoAccess
paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
statement_tex:
\label{corollaryPairwiseFactualNoAccess}
For every pair of strings $x,y$, if $\EA{+}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}(y{\in}R)}{\not\vdash}x{\in}R$, then $\EA{\not\vdash}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}(y{\in}R)}{\rightarrow}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}(x{\in}R)}$.
statement_text: For every pair of strings x,y , if EA + Con _ S + (y ∈ R) not vdash x ∈ R , then EA not vdash Con _ S + (y ∈ R) → Con _ S + (x ∈ R) .

label: conjectureConditionalFactualNoAccess
paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
statement_tex:
\label{conjectureConditionalFactualNoAccess}
Fix an admissible theory $\mathcal S$. There exists $k_{R,\mathrm{access}}^{\mathcal S}$ such that, for every $m{>}k_{R,\mathrm{access}}^{\mathcal S}$ and every $x,y{\in}\{0,1\}^m$ satisfying $x{\mathrel{\perp_R}}y$, one has $\EA{+}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}(y{\in}R)}{\not\vdash}x{\in}R$ and $\EA{+}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}(x{\in}R)}{\not\vdash}y{\in}R$.
statement_text: Fix an admissible theory S . There exists k_ R, access ^ S such that, for every m > k_ R, access ^ S and every x,y ∈ {0,1}^m satisfying x mathrel perp _R y , one has EA + Con _ S + (y ∈ R) not vdash x ∈ R and EA + Con _ S + (x ∈ R) not vdash y ∈ R .
title: bf Conditional Factual No Access

label: theoremConditionalNoAccess
paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
statement_tex:
\label{theoremConditionalNoAccess}
Assume \textbf{Conditional Factual No Access}. Then, for every $m{>}k_{R,\mathrm{access}}^{\mathcal S}$ and every $x,y{\in}\{0,1\}^m$ satisfying $x{\mathrel{\perp_R}}y$, one has $\EA{\not\vdash}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}(y{\in}R)}{\rightarrow}$ $\Con_{\mathcal S{+}(x{\in}R)}$ and $\EA{\not\vdash}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}(x{\in}R)}{\rightarrow}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}(y{\in}R)}$.
statement_text: Assume bf Conditional Factual No Access . Then, for every m > k_ R, access ^ S and every x,y ∈ {0,1}^m satisfying x mathrel perp _R y , one has EA not vdash Con _ S + (y ∈ R) → Con _ S + (x ∈ R) and EA not vdash Con _ S + (x ∈ R) → Con _ S + (y ∈ R) .

label: conjecturePairwiseSETHKFinite
paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
statement_tex:
\label{conjecturePairwiseSETHKFinite}
Fix an admissible, finitely axiomatized sequential theory $\mathcal S$. There exists $k_{R,\mathrm{hard}}^{\mathcal S}$ such that, for every $m{>}k_{R,\mathrm{hard}}^{\mathcal S}$ and every $\epsilon$ with $0{<}\epsilon{<}1$, there exists $N_{R,m,\epsilon}^{\mathcal S,\mathrm{pair}}$ such that, for every $x,y{\in}\{0,1\}^m$ satisfying $x{\mathrel{\perp_R}}y$ and every $n{>}N_{R,m,\epsilon}^{\mathcal S,\mathrm{pair}}$, one has
\[
\mathcal S{+}(y{\in}R)\vdash_{\leq 2^{(1-\epsilon)n}}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}(x{\in}R)}(n)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\EA{\vdash}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}(y{\in}R)}{\rightarrow}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}(x{\in}R)}.
\]
statement_text: Fix an admissible, finitely axiomatized sequential theory S . There exists k_ R, hard ^ S such that, for every m > k_ R, hard ^ S and every ε with 0 < ε < 1 , there exists N_ R,m,ε ^ S, pair such that, for every x,y ∈ {0,1}^m satisfying x mathrel perp _R y and every n > N_ R,m,ε ^ S, pair , one has \[ S + (y ∈ R)vdash _ ≤ 2^ (1-ε)n Con _ S + (x ∈ R) (n) quad Longleftrightarrow quad EA vdash Con _ S + (y ∈ R) → Con _ S + (x ∈ R) . \]
title: bf Pairwise SETH-K-Finite

label: theoremNoMutualHelp
paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
statement_tex:
\label{theoremNoMutualHelp}
Assume \textbf{Conditional Factual No Access} and \textbf{Pairwise SETH-K-Finite}, and let $k_{R,\mathrm{pair}}^{\mathcal S}{:=}\max\{k_{R,\mathrm{access}}^{\mathcal S},k_{R,\mathrm{hard}}^{\mathcal S}\}$. Then, for every $m{>}k_{R,\mathrm{pair}}^{\mathcal S}$ and every $\epsilon$ with $0{<}\epsilon{<}1$, there exists $N_{R,m,\epsilon}^{\mathcal S,\mathrm{pair}}$ such that, for every $x,y{\in}\{0,1\}^m$ satisfying $x{\mathrel{\perp_R}}y$ and every $n{>}N_{R,m,\epsilon}^{\mathcal S,\mathrm{pair}}$, one has $\mathcal S{+}(y{\in}R)\nvdash_{\leq 2^{(1-\epsilon)n}}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}(x{\in}R)}(n)$ and $\mathcal S{+}(x{\in}R)\nvdash_{\leq 2^{(1-\epsilon)n}}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}(y{\in}R)}(n)$.
statement_text: Assume bf Conditional Factual No Access and bf Pairwise SETH-K-Finite , and let k_ R, pair ^ S := max {k_ R, access ^ S ,k_ R, hard ^ S } . Then, for every m > k_ R, pair ^ S and every ε with 0 < ε < 1 , there exists N_ R,m,ε ^ S, pair such that, for every x,y ∈ {0,1}^m satisfying x mathrel perp _R y and every n > N_ R,m,ε ^ S, pair , one has S + (y ∈ R)nvdash _ ≤ 2^ (1-ε)n Con _ S + (x ∈ R) (n) and S + (x ∈ R)nvdash _ ≤ 2^ (1-ε)n Con _ S + (y ∈ R) (n) .

label: lemmaMutuallyRandomPairsDense
paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
statement_tex:
\label{lemmaMutuallyRandomPairsDense}
For every sufficiently large $m$, at least $(1{-}O(m^{-d}))2^{2m}$ ordered pairs $(x,y){\in}\{0,1\}^m{\times}\{0,1\}^m$ satisfy $x{\mathrel{\perp_R}}y$.
statement_text: For every sufficiently large m , at least (1 - O(m^ -d ))2^ 2m ordered pairs (x,y) ∈ {0,1}^m × {0,1}^m satisfy x mathrel perp _R y .

label: corollaryDenseNoMutualHelp
paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
statement_tex:
\label{corollaryDenseNoMutualHelp}
Assume \textbf{Conditional Factual No Access} and \textbf{Pairwise SETH-K-Finite}, and let $k_{R,\mathrm{pair}}^{\mathcal S}{:=}\max\{k_{R,\mathrm{access}}^{\mathcal S},k_{R,\mathrm{hard}}^{\mathcal S}\}$. For every sufficiently large $m{>}k_{R,\mathrm{pair}}^{\mathcal S}$ and every $\epsilon$ with $0{<}\epsilon{<}1$, there exists $N_{R,m,\epsilon}^{\mathcal S,\mathrm{pair}}$ such that, for every $n{>}N_{R,m,\epsilon}^{\mathcal S,\mathrm{pair}}$, at least $(1{-}O(m^{-d}))2^{2m}$ ordered pairs $(x,y){\in}\{0,1\}^m{\times}\{0,1\}^m$ satisfy $\mathcal S{+}(y{\in}R)\nvdash_{\leq 2^{(1-\epsilon)n}}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}(x{\in}R)}(n)$ and $\mathcal S{+}(x{\in}R)\nvdash_{\leq 2^{(1-\epsilon)n}}\Con_{\mathcal S{+}(y{\in}R)}(n)$.
statement_text: Assume bf Conditional Factual No Access and bf Pairwise SETH-K-Finite , and let k_ R, pair ^ S := max {k_ R, access ^ S ,k_ R, hard ^ S } . For every sufficiently large m > k_ R, pair ^ S and every ε with 0 < ε < 1 , there exists N_ R,m,ε ^ S, pair such that, for every n > N_ R,m,ε ^ S, pair , at least (1 - O(m^ -d ))2^ 2m ordered pairs (x,y) ∈ {0,1}^m × {0,1}^m satisfy S + (y ∈ R)nvdash _ ≤ 2^ (1-ε)n Con _ S + (x ∈ R) (n) and S + (x ∈ R)nvdash _ ≤ 2^ (1-ε)n Con _ S + (y ∈ R) (n) .

label: lem:finite-ph-coding
paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
statement_tex:
\label{lem:finite-ph-coding}
For every $i{\geq}1$ and every polynomial time bound $t$, the predicate $Q_i^t$ lies uniformly in $\Pi_{i+1}^p$. Moreover, if $\Pi_i^p{=}\Pi_{i+1}^p$, then $Q_i^t$ is decidable by a polynomial-time Turing machine with oracle access to $\Pi_i^p$.
statement_text: For every i ≥ 1 and every polynomial time bound t , the predicate Q_i^t lies uniformly in Π_ i+1 ^p . Moreover, if Π_i^p = Π_ i+1 ^p , then Q_i^t is decidable by a polynomial-time Turing machine with oracle access to Π_i^p .

label: ass:algph
paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
statement_tex:
\label{ass:algph}
For every $i{\geq}1$, there exists a polynomial time bound $t_i$ such that the canonical finite predicate $Q_i^{t_i}$, whose YES-set is $\widehat R_i^{t_i}$, is not decidable by any polynomial-time Turing machine with oracle access to $\Pi_i^p$.
statement_text: For every i ≥ 1 , there exists a polynomial time bound t_i such that the canonical finite predicate Q_i^ t_i , whose YES-set is widehat R_i^ t_i , is not decidable by any polynomial-time Turing machine with oracle access to Π_i^p .
title: bf SETH-K-PH

label: thm:phnoncollapse

label: thm:ph-density
paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
statement_tex:
\label{thm:ph-density}
Assume \textbf{SETH-K-PH}. For every $i{\geq}1$, let $t_i$ be the time bound supplied by the assumption. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)}]
\item \emph{(Explicitness.)} The predicate $Q_i^{t_i}$ is an explicit language in $\Pi_{i+1}^p{\setminus}\PP^{\Pi_i^p}$. In particular, it witnesses $\Pi_i^p{\neq}\Pi_{i+1}^p$.
\item \emph{(Density.)} Its YES-set $\widehat R_i^{t_i}$ has density at least $1{-}n^{-d}$ inside $\{0,1\}^n$. Thus almost every length-$n$ string is a YES-instance.
\item \emph{(Sparse-side localization.)} Every polynomial-time $\Pi_i^p$-oracle machine that is correct on all of $\widehat R_i^{t_i}$ for all sufficiently large $n$ must err, for infinitely many $n$, on some string in the sparse complement $\overline{\widehat R_i^{t_i}}$.
\end{enumerate}
statement_text: Assume bf SETH-K-PH . For every i ≥ 1 , let t_i be the time bound supplied by the assumption. Then: (Explicitness.) The predicate Q_i^ t_i is an explicit language in Π_ i+1 ^p \ P ^ Π_i^p . In particular, it witnesses Π_i^p ≠ Π_ i+1 ^p . (Density.) Its YES-set widehat R_i^ t_i has density at least 1 - n^ -d inside {0,1}^n . Thus almost every length- n string is a YES-instance. (Sparse-side localization.) Every polynomial-time Π_i^p -oracle machine that is correct on all of widehat R_i^ t_i for all sufficiently large n must err, for infinitely many n , on some string in the sparse complement overline widehat R_i^ t_i .

statement_tex:
\label{def:boundary-exposure-main}

statement_text: For a theory S and a threshold N , let E_ S (x,N) := ∃ m ≤ N ¬ Con _ S + (x ∈ R) (m) . Equivalently, E_ S (x,N) holds if there is a contradiction proof of length at most N from the extension S + (x ∈ R) .

label: thm:liu-pass-main
paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
statement_tex:
\label{thm:liu-pass-main}
For every polynomial time bound $t$ satisfying $t(n){\geq}(1{+}\delta)n$ for some constant $\delta{>}0$, one-way functions exist if and only if $K^t$ is mildly hard on average over the uniform distribution: there is a polynomial $p$ such that no probabilistic polynomial-time algorithm computes $K^t(x)$ correctly on more than a $1{-}1/p(n)$ fraction of strings $x{\in}\{0,1\}^n$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
statement_text: For every polynomial time bound t satisfying t(n) ≥ (1 + δ)n for some constant δ > 0 , one-way functions exist if and only if K^t is mildly hard on average over the uniform distribution: there is a polynomial p such that no probabilistic polynomial-time algorithm computes K^t(x) correctly on more than a 1 - 1/p(n) fraction of strings x ∈ {0,1}^n for all sufficiently large n .
title: Liu--Pass

paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
statement_tex:
\label{ass:avg-boundary-reflection-main}
There exist a computable polynomial time bound $t$, a polynomial $N(n)$, and a polynomial-time samplable ensemble $\mathcal D{=}\{D_n\}$ supported on $R_t{\cap}\{0,1\}^n$ such that both $\Pr_{x\sim D_n}[x{\in}R]$ and $\Pr_{x\sim D_n}[x{\in}R_t{\setminus}R]$ are bounded away from $0$ uniformly in $n$, and such that the following reflection principle holds: if some probabilistic polynomial-time algorithm decides $E_{\mathcal S}(x,N(n))$ on $x{\sim}D_n$ with success probability $1{-}o(1)$, then for almost every $x{\sim}D_n$ with $x{\in}R$, one has $\EA{+}\Con_{\mathcal S}{\vdash}x{\in}R$.
statement_text: There exist a computable polynomial time bound t , a polynomial N(n) , and a polynomial-time samplable ensemble D = {D_n} supported on R_t ∩ {0,1}^n such that both Pr _ x D_n [x ∈ R] and Pr _ x D_n [x ∈ R_t \ R] are bounded away from 0 uniformly in n , and such that the following reflection principle holds: if some probabilistic polynomial-time algorithm decides E_ S (x,N(n)) on x D_n with success probability 1 - o(1) , then for almost every x D_n with x ∈ R , one has EA + Con _ S vdash x ∈ R .

statement_tex:
\label{prop:avg-boundary-hardness-main}

label: ass:boundary-calibration-main
paper_title: Hardness as an Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
statement_tex:
\label{ass:boundary-calibration-main}
The ensemble $\mathcal D$, the threshold $N(n)$, and the time bound $t$ are chosen so that two conditions hold. First, on $\mathcal D$ the boundary-exposure predicate $E_{\mathcal S}(\cdot,N(n))$ tracks $t$-time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity up to a polynomial-time computable reindexing. Second, this correspondence bridges $\mathcal D$ to the uniform distribution on which Liu--Pass operates: any average-case algorithm computing $\Kt$ over the uniform distribution on $\{0,1\}^n$ that is strong enough to violate the Liu--Pass hardness condition yields, through the reindexing, a $1{-}o(1)$-success heuristic for $E_{\mathcal S}(\cdot,N(n))$ on $x{\sim}D_n$.
statement_text: The ensemble D , the threshold N(n) , and the time bound t are chosen so that two conditions hold. First, on D the boundary-exposure predicate E_ S ( · ,N(n)) tracks t -time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity up to a polynomial-time computable reindexing. Second, this correspondence bridges D to the uniform distribution on which Liu--Pass operates: any average-case algorithm computing K^ t over the uniform distribution on {0,1}^n that is strong enough to violate the Liu--Pass hardness condition yields, through the reindexing, a 1 - o(1) -success heuristic for E_ S ( · ,N(n)) on x D_n .

label: infthm:main
paper_title: Towards Worst-case Hardness for Low-Noise LPN
statement_tex:
\label{infthm:main}
  Suppose there is an efficient algorithm that has non-negligible advantage in solving LPN with $n$ variables, $t$ samples, and noise rate $n^{-\alpha}$ for some constant $\alpha < 1$. Then, for any constant $\beta > 0$ such that $\alpha + \beta < 1$, and $m = O(t^2n^{2\beta})$, there are efficient algorithms $\algS$ and $\algD$ such that, for any $A\in\F_2^{m\times n}$, either $\algS$ can decode the code generated by $A$ from random noise of rate $n^{-(\alpha+\beta)}$, or $\algD$ can distinguish noisy codewords of the dual of this code from random for noise rate $n^\beta/m$.

Then, for any constant β > 0 such that α + β < 1 , and m = O(t^2n^ 2β ) , there are efficient algorithms algS and algD such that, for any A ∈ F _2^ m × n , either algS can decode the code generated by A from random noise of rate n^ -(α+β) , or algD can distinguish noisy codewords of the dual of this code from random for noise rate n^β/m .

paper_title: Towards Worst-case Hardness for Low-Noise LPN
statement_tex:
Let $n,m \in \mathbb{Z}$, and $\eta \in [0, 1]$. For sample count $m$, secret dimension $n$, and noise parameter $\eta$, algorithms $\Slpn$ and $\Dlpn$ are said to have advantage $\eps \in [0, 1]$ in solving the \emph{Search LPN} and \emph{Decision LPN} problems, respectively, if they satisfy the following conditions:
    \begin{itemize}[itemsep=0pt]
        \item \emph{Search LPN:} $\Slpn$ recovers the secret $s$ with probability at least $\eps$:
        \[
            \Pr_{\substack{A \gets \Field{2}^{m \times n} \\ s \gets \Field{2}^n \\ e \gets \mathrm{Ber}(\eta)^m}}[\Slpn(A, As + e) = s] \geq \eps
       . \]
        
        \item \emph{Decision LPN:} $\Dlpn$ distinguishes LPN samples from uniform with advantage at least $\eps$:
        \[
            \abs{\Pr_{\substack{A \gets \Field{2}^{m \times n} \\ s \gets \Field{2}^n \\ e \gets \mathrm{Ber}(\eta)^m}}[\Dlpn(A, As + e) = 1] - \Pr_{\substack{A \gets \Field{2}^{m \times n} \\ b \gets \Field{2}^m}}[\Dlpn(A, b) = 1]} \geq \eps.
        \]
    \end{itemize}

For sample count m , secret dimension n , and noise parameter η , algorithms algS _ LPN and algD _ LPN are said to have advantage ε ∈ [0, 1] in solving the Search LPN and Decision LPN problems, respectively, if they satisfy the following conditions: Search LPN: algS _ LPN recovers the secret s with probability at least ε : \[ Pr _ substack A gets F _ 2 ^ m × n s gets F _ 2 ^n e gets Ber (η)^m [ algS _ LPN (A, As + e) = s] ≥ ε . \] Decision LPN: algD _ LPN distinguishes LPN samples from uniform with advantage at least ε : \[ abs Pr _ substack A gets F _ 2 ^ m × n s gets F _ 2 ^n e gets Ber (η)^m [ algD _ LPN (A, As + e) = 1] - Pr _ substack A gets F _ 2 ^ m × n b gets F _ 2 ^m [ algD _ LPN (A, b) = 1] ≥ ε. \]

statement_tex:
Let $n,m \in \mathbb{Z}$, and $\theta \in [0, 1]$. For code length $m$, code dimension $n$, and noise parameter $\theta$, algorithms $\Ssd$ and $\Dsd$ are said to have advantage $\eps \in [0, 1]$ in solving the \emph{Search SD} and \emph{Decision SD} problems, respectively, if they satisfy the following conditions:
    \begin{itemize}[itemsep=0pt]
        \item \emph{Search SD:} $\Ssd$ decodes a syndrome with probability at least $\eps$:
        \[
            \Pr_{\substack{A \gets \Field{2}^{m \times n}\\ r \gets \mathcal{W}(m, \theta \cdot m)}}[\Ssd(A, r^TA) = r] \geq \eps.
        \]
        
        \item \emph{Decision SD:} $\Dsd$ distinguishes a syndrome from uniform with advantage at least $\eps$:
        \[
            \abs{\Pr_{\substack{A \gets \Field{2}^{m \times n}\\ r \gets \mathcal{W}(m, \theta \cdot m)}}[\Dsd(A, r^TA) = 1] - \Pr_{\substack{A \gets \Field{2}^{m \times n} \\ c \gets \Field{2}^n}}[\Dsd(A, c^T) = 1]} \geq \eps.
        \]
    \end{itemize}

For code length m , code dimension n , and noise parameter θ , algorithms algS _ SD and algD _ SD are said to have advantage ε ∈ [0, 1] in solving the Search SD and Decision SD problems, respectively, if they satisfy the following conditions: Search SD: algS _ SD decodes a syndrome with probability at least ε : \[ Pr _ substack A gets F _ 2 ^ m × n r gets W (m, θ · m) [ algS _ SD (A, r^TA) = r] ≥ ε. \] Decision SD: algD _ SD distinguishes a syndrome from uniform with advantage at least ε : \[ abs Pr _ substack A gets F _ 2 ^ m × n r gets W (m, θ · m) [ algD _ SD (A, r^TA) = 1] - Pr _ substack A gets F _ 2 ^ m × n c gets F _ 2 ^n [ algD _ SD (A, c^T) = 1] ≥ ε. \]

label: thm:main
paper_title: Towards Worst-case Hardness for Low-Noise LPN
statement_tex:
\label{thm:main}
  Consider $n, m, t \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $\eta, \theta \in (0,1)$ such that $t^2\theta^2m < 1$. Suppose there exists an algorithm for Search LPN with sample count $t$, secret dimension $n$, and noise parameter $\tau =  (1 - (1-2\eta)^{\theta \cdot m})/2$, which runs in time $T$ and has advantage $\eps$. Then there exist algorithms $\algD$ and $\algS$ such that for every matrix $A \in \Field{2}^{m \times n}$, at least one of the following is true:
  \begin{itemize}[itemsep=0pt]
    \item $\algS$ runs in  time $\poly\left(n, m, T, (1/\eps)^{\log_m(m/\eps)}\right)$ and decodes codewords of $A$ from random noise such that, \[\Pr_{\substack{s \gets \Field{2}^n\\ e \gets Ber(\eta)^m}}[\algS(A, As+e) = s^\prime\  \mathrm{and}\  \wt(As^\prime - (As + e)) \leq 2\eta m] \geq \eps/2 - o(\eps).
    \]
    \item $\algD$ runs in time $\poly(n,m) + T$ and distinguishes a sparse combination of rows of $A$ from a uniform string such that,
    \[
    \Pr_{c \gets \Field{2}^n}[\algD(A, c^T) = 1] - \Pr_{r \gets {\cW(m,\theta \cdot m)}}[\algD(A, r^TA) = 1]  \geq \eps/2t.
    \]
  \end{itemize}
statement_text: Consider n, m, t ∈ Z and η, θ ∈ (0,1) such that t^2θ^2m < 1 . Suppose there exists an algorithm for Search LPN with sample count t , secret dimension n , and noise parameter τ = (1 - (1-2η)^ θ · m )/2 , which runs in time T and has advantage ε . Then there exist algorithms algD and algS such that for every matrix A ∈ F _ 2 ^ m × n , at least one of the following is true: algS runs in time poly (n, m, T, (1/ε)^ log _m(m/ε) ) and decodes codewords of A from random noise such that, \[Pr _ substack s gets F _ 2 ^n e gets Ber(η)^m [algS (A, As+e) = s^prime \ and \ wt (As^prime - (As + e)) ≤ 2η m] ≥ ε/2 - o(ε). \] algD runs in time poly (n,m) + T and distinguishes a sparse combination of rows of A from a uniform string such that, \[ Pr _ c gets F _ 2 ^n [algD (A, c^T) = 1] - Pr _ r gets cW (m,θ · m) [algD (A, r^TA) = 1] ≥ ε/2t. \]

label: cor:lpnmain
paper_title: Towards Worst-case Hardness for Low-Noise LPN
statement_tex:
\label{cor:lpnmain}
    Consider any polynomial $t(n) \in \mathbb{Z}$ with $t(n) > n$, constants $\alpha, \beta \in (0.01, 0.99)$ with $\alpha + \beta \in (0.01, 0.99)$, and $m(n) = \ceil{2t^2n^{2\beta}}$. Suppose that for every pair of PPT algorithms $(\algS, \algD)$, there exists a negligible function $negl$ such that, for all large enough $n$, there exists an $\F_2$-matrix $A$ of dimension $m \times n$ for which both of these conditions are true: 
    \begin{itemize}[itemsep=0pt]
        \item $\Pr[\algS(A, As+e) = s^\prime\  \mathrm{and}\  \wt(As^\prime - (As + e)) \leq 2 m/n^{\alpha+\beta}]  \leq negl(n)$, where $s \gets \Field{2}^n$, $e \gets Ber(n^{-(\alpha + \beta)})^{m}$.
        \item $\abs{\Pr[\algD(A, c^T) = 1] - \Pr[\algD(A, r^TA) = 1]} \leq negl(n)$, where $c \gets \Field{2}^n, r \gets \cW(m,n^{\beta})$.
    \end{itemize}    
    Then, for the Search LPN problem with sample count $t(n)$, secret dimension $n$, and noise parameter $n^{-\alpha}$, no PPT algorithm has non-negligible advantage.

label: lem:merge_reduce
paper_title: Towards Tight Bounds for Streaming Attention
statement_tex:
\label{lem:merge_reduce}
   Fix $n, \gamma, U, V$. Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an offline algorithm which receives $K \subset U$  as input, and outputs $\widetilde{K} \subset K$ such that $|\widetilde{K}| \leq |K|/2$ and for any $q \in V$, with probability $1 - \frac{1}{\poly n}$, 
   \begin{equation*}
       \left|\gamma(K, q) - 2\gamma(\widetilde{K}, q)\right| \leq \eta
   \end{equation*}
   for some error bound $\eta =  \eta(|K|)$.
   Let $T = T(|K|)$ be a deterministic upper bound on the runtime of $\mathcal{A}$. 
   Then for every block size $b \geq 1$, there is a streaming algorithm that processes a stream $k_1,  \cdots, k_n$ and, at every time step $j$, maintains a weighted coreset $C_j$ for the prefix $K_j = (k_1, \cdots, k_j)$ such that the following holds: 
    
    For any $q \in U$, with probability $1-\frac{1}{\poly n}$,
   \[\left|
  \gamma(K_j,q)-\gamma(C_j,q)\right|
   \leq O\qty(\eta(b) \cdot \frac{j}{b} \log\frac{j}{b}), \]
   where $\gamma(C_j,q) := \sum_{x \in C_j} w_x \gamma(x,q)$
   for $w_x$ denoting the weight of $x$ in the coreset $C_j$.
   
Moreover, $|C_j|  = O\left(b\log\frac{j}{b}\right)$. The streaming algorithm uses $\tilde{O}\left(b\log\frac{j}{b}\right )$ bits of storage space and $O\left(T(b)\cdot \log\frac{j}{b}\right)$ update time.

Let T = T(|K|) be a deterministic upper bound on the runtime of A . Then for every block size b ≥ 1 , there is a streaming algorithm that processes a stream k_1, ... , k_n and, at every time step j , maintains a weighted coreset C_j for the prefix K_j = (k_1, ... , k_j) such that the following holds: For any q ∈ U , with probability 1-frac 1 poly n , \[ | γ(K_j,q)-γ(C_j,q) | ≤ Oqty (η(b) · frac j b log frac j b ), \] where γ(C_j,q) := Σ _ x ∈ C_j w_x γ(x,q) for w_x denoting the weight of x in the coreset C_j . Moreover, |C_j| = O (b log frac j b ) . The streaming algorithm uses tilde O (b log frac j b ) bits of storage space and O (T(b) · log frac j b ) update time.

    Moreover, $ \sum_{k \in K_j} \psi_1(k)$ can be stored in $\tilde{O}\Bigl(\frac{(d+t)^{t}}{t!}\Bigr)$ bits of space, and can be updated in $\tilde{O}\Bigl(\frac{(d+t)^{t}}{t!}\Bigr)$  time

\label{lem:coreset}
Let  $t$ be an integer such that $0 \leq t \leq d$.  There is a streaming algorithm that processes a stream $K = (k_1,  \cdots, k_n) \subset \mathcal{B}_r$ and, at every time step $j$,  maintains a weighted coreset $C_j$ for the prefix $K_j = (k_1, \cdots, k_j)$ such that the following holds:

     \]

statement_tex:
{lemma}{certifyball}[Certify]\label{cor:certify-ball}
There is a randomized procedure that, given a set
\(K \subseteq B(c,r)\) and parameters \(\Delta,\tau,\delta \in \left(0,\tfrac13\right)\), runs in time
\[
O\!\left(\frac{d}{\Delta^{2}\tau}\log\!\left(\frac{2|K|}{\delta}\right)\cdot |K|\right)
\]
and, with probability at least \(1-\delta\), does one of the following:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item returns a point \(k^* \in B(c,r)\) such that
    \[
    \left|B\!\left(k^*, \sqrt{1-\Delta^4}\,r\right)\cap K\right|
    \;\ge\;
    \Omega(\Delta^2)\cdot \tau |K|,
    \]
    \item certifies that \(K\) is \((\Delta',\tau)\)-pseudo-random, where \(\Delta'=\Theta(\Delta)\).
\end{enumerate}
We refer to this procedure as \(\Certify_{\Delta,\tau,\delta}\).

statement_tex:
\label{lem:merge-reduce-w}    Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a black-box offline algorithm which takes as input a dataset $K \subset B(0,r)$, $|K| \leq n$,  and returns $\widetilde{K} \subset K$, $|\widetilde{K}| \leq 3|K|/4$, weight function $\alpha_x \in \{1, 2\}$ such that with probability $1 - \frac{1}{\poly n}$, for any fixed $q \in B(0, r)$,
\begin{align}\label{eq:error_bound-mr}
\left|\exp(K, q) - \exp(\tilde{K}, \alpha,  q)\right| \leq O\left(e^{r^2(1 + o(1))}\cdot n^{o(1)}\cdot \frac{\exp(K, q)}{|K|}\right).
\end{align}
   
   Let $T(m)$ denote the runtime $\mathcal{A}$ on inputs of size $m$. Assume that the space complexity of $\mathcal{A}$ is $O(m)$.

   Algorithm $\mathcal{A}$ can be adapted to process $K$ as a stream. At every step $j$ of the stream, it maintains a weighted coreset $C_j$ of the $j$ first elements of the stream $K_j$. Let $w_x^j$ denote the weight of a point $x \in C_j$ and $w^j$~-- the weight function. We have with probability $1-\frac{1}{\poly (n)}$, for any fixed $q \in U$ and desired error $\epsilon \in (0, 1)$,
   \[\left|
  \exp(K_j,q)-\exp(C_j, w^j, q)\right|
   \leq \epsilon \cdot \exp(K_j, q).
   \]
The size of the coreset, runtime and memory are defined in terms of the \textit{block size} of the algorithm $b$
\[
|C_j| \leq O\left(b\log^2\left(\frac{|K_j|}{b}\right)\right), \quad \text{ runtime} =  O\left(T(b)\cdot \log^2\left(\frac{|K_j|}{b}\right)\right), \quad \text{ space}=
   O\left(b\log^2\left(\frac{|K_j|}{b}\right)\right),
   \]
and the block size $b$ is defined by the desired error $\epsilon$ 
   \[
   b = \frac{e^{r^2(1 + o(1))}\cdot n^{o(1)}}{\epsilon}.
   \]

label: lem:weighted_streaming_coreset

statement_tex:
\label{lem:weighted_streaming_coreset}
    Let $U \times V\subset   \R^d \times \R^d $ be a predefined subset of the domain. There is a randomized algorithm $\BaseCompress'$ which receives as inputs $K \subset U$ and any weights $\{w(k)\}_{k\in K}$ with $|w(k)| \leq 1$ . $\BaseCompress'(K, \{w(k)\}_{k\in K})$ outputs $\widetilde{K} \subset K$ such that $|\widetilde{K}| \leq |K|/2$ and for any $q \in V$, with probability $1 - \delta$,
           \[\left|\expker(K, w, q) - 2\expker(\widetilde{K}, w, q)\right| \leq O\left(\sqrt{\max_{u \in U}\expker(u, u)\cdot \max_{v \in V}\expker(v, v)}\cdot \log (|K|/\delta)\right).\]
    $\BaseCompress'(K,w)$ runs in $O(|K|^2 \cdot T)$ time, where $T$ is the maximum time to access $\expker(k,q)$.

label: def:random-kde-instance
paper_title: Towards Tight Bounds for Streaming Attention
statement_text: Let x ∈ {0,1}^ 2n be a binary vector with exactly n ones. Let K ⊂ R ^d be a set of 2n points drawn i.i.d.\ from a rotationally invariant distribution, independently of x . Let K_ x be the set of points indexed by the ones of x . A random KDE instance is an instance of the streaming KDE problem (cref def:streaming-kde ) in which the keys k_1, ... , k_n are the points in K and the query q is chosen from K . Vector q is chosen to be one of the keys k_i ∈ K ; the position in the dataset i is independent of the randomness of K .

label: lemma:certify
paper_title: Towards Tight Bounds for Streaming Attention
statement_tex:
\label{lemma:certify}
There is a randomized procedure that, given a set
$K \subseteq S^{d-1}$ and parameters $\Delta,\tau,\delta \in \left(0,\tfrac13\right)$, runs in time
\[
O\!\left(\frac{d}{\Delta^{2}\tau}\log\!\left(\frac{2|K|}{\delta}\right)\cdot |K|\right)
\]
and, with probability at least $1-\delta$, does one of the following:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item returns a point $k^* \in S^{d-1}$ such that
    \[
    \left|B\!\left(k^*, \sqrt{2(1 - \Delta^2)}\right)\cap K\right|
    \;\ge\;
    \Omega(\Delta^2)\cdot \tau |K|
    \]
    \item or certifies that the set $K$ is $(\Delta',\tau)$-pseudo-random, where $\Delta' = \Theta(\Delta)$.
\end{enumerate}
statement_text: There is a randomized procedure that, given a set K ⊆ S^ d-1 and parameters Δ,τ,δ ∈ (0,tfrac 13 ) , runs in time \[ O (frac d Δ^ 2 τ log (frac 2|K| δ ) · |K| ) \] and, with probability at least 1-δ , does one of the following: returns a point k^* ∈ S^ d-1 such that \[ |B (k^*, sqrt 2(1 - Δ^2) ) ∩ K | ≥ Ω(Δ^2) · τ |K| \] or certifies that the set K is (Δ',τ) -pseudo-random, where Δ' = Θ(Δ) .

statement_tex:
\label{informalthm:samplable-nature}
Let $\cF$ be a class of VC dimension $d$. Then, there exists a single algorithm that, given a realizable ERM oracle for $\cF$, runs in time $\poly(T^d, p(T))$ and, for every $p$-time samplable $\dist^\star$ and every $f^\star \in \cF$, achieves $o(T)$ regret, where the rate depends only on $\dist^\star$ and $d$.
statement_text: Let cF be a class of VC dimension d . Then, there exists a single algorithm that, given a realizable ERM oracle for cF , runs in time poly (T^d, p(T)) and, for every p -time samplable P^star and every f^star ∈ cF , achieves o(T) regret, where the rate depends only on P^star and d .

statement_tex:
\label{assumption:p-star}

statement_text: The learner has access to a simulatable process P that approximates P^star . That is, the learner has access to an oracle O _ P that, when queried, returns an independent sample (a trajectory (X_1, ... ,X_T) ) from P . We refer to P simply as the simulator.

label: lemma:rel-admissibility
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_tex:
{lemma}{RelAdmissibility}
    \label{lemma:rel-admissibility}
    Let $\cF$ be an arbitrary function class, and consider any $t \le T$. Suppose the simulator is exact, that is $\dist = \dist^\star$, and let $q_t$ be as in~\cref{eq:relaxation-mgf-strategy}. Then, for any history $\seq S_{1:t-1}$, we have
\[
\En_{X_t \sim \dist_t^\star(\cdot \mid \seq X_{1:t-1})} \exp\left( \sup_{Y_t}\left[\eta \En_{\hat  Y_t \sim  q_t} \ind\{ \hat Y_t  \neq Y_t\} + \eta \rel(\seq S_{1:t})\right] \right) \le \exp\left( \eta \rel(\seq S_{1:t-1}) \right).
\]
Thus, conditioned on $\seq S_{1:t-1}$, $\En_{X_t} \sup_{Y_t} \Phi_t \le \Phi_{t-1}$, and therefore, $\{\Phi_t\}_{t \le T}$ is a supermartingale.
statement_text: lemma RelAdmissibility Let cF be an arbitrary function class, and consider any t ≤ T . Suppose the simulator is exact, that is P = P^star , and let q_t be as in cref eq:relaxation-mgf-strategy . Then, for any history S_ 1:t-1 , we have \[ E _ X_t P_t^star ( · mid X_ 1:t-1 ) exp ( sup _ Y_t [η E _ hat Y_t q_t m 1 { hat Y_t ≠ Y_t} + η Rel (S_ 1:t ) ] ) ≤ exp ( η Rel (S_ 1:t-1 ) ). \] Thus, conditioned on S_ 1:t-1 , E _ X_t sup _ Y_t Φ_t ≤ Φ_ t-1 , and therefore, {Φ_t}_ t ≤ T is a supermartingale.

Then, q_t as in cref eq:relaxation-mgf-strategy can be written as \[ q_t(S_ 1:t-1 , X_t) = frac 1 2 + frac 1 2η log (frac E exp (η G _ 1 (W^t)) E exp (η G _ 0 (W^t)) ) \]

label: lemma:mse-bound
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_tex:
{lemma}{MSEBound}
    \label{lemma:mse-bound}
    For an arbitrary history $\seq S_{1:t-1}$, an arbitrary covariate $X_t$, and $\eta\le 1$, we have
    \[
    \En\left[(\hat q_t - q_t)^2\right] \lesssim \frac{\nvar}{N},
    \quad \text{where} \quad
    \nvar := \max_{y \in \{0,1\}} \frac{\En \exp(2\eta \off{y}(\seq W^t))}{\left(\En \exp(\eta \off{y}(\seq W^t))\right)^2},
    \]
    is the normalized variance of the exponential moment.
statement_text: lemma MSEBound For an arbitrary history S_ 1:t-1 , an arbitrary covariate X_t , and η ≤ 1 , we have \[ E [(hat q_t - q_t)^2 ] lesssim frac v_t N , quad where quad v_t := max _ y ∈ {0,1} frac E exp (2η G _ y (W^t)) ( E exp (η G _ y (W^t)) )^2 , \] is the normalized variance of the exponential moment.

label: lemma:v-eta
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_tex:
{lemma}{VEtaBound}
\label{lemma:v-eta}
    For an arbitrary history $\seq S_{1:t-1}$, an arbitrary covariate $X_t$, and $\eta\le 1$, we have
    \[
    \nvar \le \exp(2\eta) \En \exp\left(2\eta \sup_{f} \sum_{s= t+1}^T \varepsilon_s \frac{2f(X_s) - 1}{2}\right) \lesssim 
    \exp\left(O(\eta \sqrt{dT} + \eta^2 T)\right).
    \]
statement_text: lemma VEtaBound For an arbitrary history S_ 1:t-1 , an arbitrary covariate X_t , and η ≤ 1 , we have \[ v_t ≤ exp (2η) E exp (2η sup _ f Σ _ s= t+1 ^T ε_s frac 2f(X_s) - 1 2 ) lesssim exp (O(η sqrt dT + η^2 T) ). \]

Then, an algorithm that plays according to cref eq:plug-in with N samples per step and inverse temperature η achieves the following regret bound E _ P^star Reg (cF ,T) lesssim sqrt dT + η T + frac 1 η KL dvr * P^star P + T sqrt frac exp (O(η sqrt dT + η^2 T)) N .

label: cor:sim-families
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_text: corollary LearnabilitySublinearKL Let cP be a family of processes with cR (cP ) ≤ o(T) , and cF a bounded VC dimension class. paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_tex:
\label[definition]{def:samplable}
    Let $p \colon \mathbb N \to \mathbb N$ be a time bound. Then, distribution $P \in \Delta(\Sigma^\infty)$ is $p$-time samplable iff there exists a program $\pi$ such that, for every $t \ge 1$ and $s \sim \Unif(\{0,1\}^{p(t)})$, we have $ U^{p(t)}(\pi, 1^{t}\# s) \sim P_{1:t}.$
    For a distribution $P \in \Delta(\Sigma^\infty)$, let
    \[
    K^p(P) = \min\left\{|\pi| \colon U^{p(t)}(\pi, 1^{t}\# s) \sim P_{1:t} \text{ for every } t \ge 1, \text{ where } s \sim \Unif(\{0,1\}^{p(t)}) \right\}
    \]
    be the (time-bounded) Kolmogorov complexity of $P$ if $P$ is $p$-time samplable.
statement_text: Let p colon N → N be a time bound. Then, distribution P ∈ Δ(Σ^ ∞ ) is p -time samplable iff there exists a program π such that, for every t ≥ 1 and s Unif ({0,1}^ p(t) ) , we have U^ p(t) (π, 1^ t \# s) P_ 1:t . For a distribution P ∈ Δ(Σ^ ∞ ) , let \[ K^p(P) = min {|π| colon U^ p(t) (π, 1^ t \# s) P_ 1:t for every t ≥ 1, where s Unif ({0,1}^ p(t) ) } \] be the (time-bounded) Kolmogorov complexity of P if P is p -time samplable.
title: Time-bounded samplable distribution

label: thm:universal-dist
paper_title: Learning with Simulators: No Regret in a Computationally Bounded World
statement_text: theorem UniversalDist Let p colon N → N be a time-constructible bound. There exists a time bound p'(t) = poly (p(t)) and a sequence of measures {μ^t}_ t ≥ 1 , with each μ^t ∈ Δ (Σ^*) samplable in time p'(t) that satisfy the following. For any p -time samplable distribution P and any x ∈ cX ^t we have \[ log frac P_ 1:t (le x rangle ) μ^t(le xrangle ) ≤ K^p(P) + 2 log K^p(P) + O(1). \]

label: thm:samplable-nature
